title: Prevalence of Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Cameroon: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a global public health problem, and many regions of Sub-Saharan Africa are disproportionately affected, including Cameroon, where prevalence has previously been shown to be high. This study aimed to provide up-to-date estimates of HBV prevalence in Cameroon. We searched Medline, Global Health, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Africa Index Medicus and the Journal of Health Science and Disease at the University of Yaounde. We included studies reporting HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence in the general population and subpopulations. A random-effects meta-analysis was used to generate pooled estimates of HBsAg prevalence, overall and for population subgroups including those considered at relatively higher-risk and relatively lower-risk of HBV infection. Heterogeneity was assessed using the index of heterogeneity (I 2 ). Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool. Out of 1236 records, 92 papers with 100 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Overall prevalence of HBV in Cameroon was 9.98% (95% confidence interval [CI] 9.00-11.02) with high heterogeneity (I 2 = 98.10%). The prevalences for relatively lower-risk and higher-risk populations were8.94% (95% CI 7.84-10.11) and 12.70% (95% CI 10.28-15.32), respectively. In subgroup analyses, we found that sex, geographical area (regions), population risk groups and study design were the main sources of heterogeneity. Overall, HBV prevalence remains high in Cameroon. Our findings suggest an urgent need for health interventions to halt the spread of the disease, with particular attention needed for males and regions with the highest prevalence.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in Cameroon, focusing on the central question of estimating HBV prevalence in the general population and subpopulations using HBsAg seropositivity as the diagnostic marker.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis that searched Medline, Global Health, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Africa Index Medicus, and the Journal of Health Science and Disease at the University of Yaounde. Eligible studies reported HBsAg prevalence in the general population and subpopulations, assessed using a random-effects meta-analysis with heterogeneity quantified by I2 and study quality evaluated via the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool. A total of 92 papers with 100 studies were included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled overall HBV prevalence in Cameroon is 9.98% (95% CI 9.00–11.02) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 98.10%). Prevalence is higher in relatively higher-risk populations (12.70%, 95% CI 10.28–15.32) compared to relatively lower-risk populations (8.94%, 95% CI 7.84–10.11). Subgroup analyses identified sex, geographical area (regions), population risk groups, and study design as major sources of heterogeneity.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review reports substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 98.10%) that remains largely unexplained despite subgroup analyses, indicating potential unmeasured confounders or methodological inconsistencies across included studies. The high heterogeneity limits the precision of pooled estimates and complicates interpretation of regional and population-specific differences.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings underscore the need for targeted public health interventions, particularly for males and regions with the highest HBV prevalence, to reduce transmission and improve control measures in Cameroon. Standardized study designs and reporting across future prevalence studies are required to address heterogeneity and improve comparability.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis provides updated estimates of hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevalence in Cameroon, reporting an overall pooled prevalence of 9.98% (95% CI 9.00–11.02) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 98.10%). Prevalence is higher in higher-risk populations (12.70%) than in lower-risk populations (8.94%). Subgroup analyses indicate that sex, geographical area, population risk group, and study design are key sources of heterogeneity. The review highlights the urgent need for targeted interventions, especially among males and in high-prevalence regions, and calls for standardized methodologies in future prevalence studies to reduce heterogeneity and improve comparability.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了喀麦隆的人类 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染情况,重点关注使用 HBsAg 血清阳性作为诊断标志物估计普通人群和亚人群中 HBV 患病率 的核心问题。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一项系统综述和荟萃分析,检索了 Medline、Global Health、Embase、Web of Science、Cochrane Library、Africa Index Medicus 以及雅温得大学的《健康科学与疾病杂志》。符合条件的研究报告了一般人群和亚人群中的 HBsAg 患病率,使用随机效应荟萃分析进行评估,异质性通过 I2 量化,研究质量通过 Joanna Briggs Institute 关键评估工具进行评估。共纳入 92 篇论文、100 项研究。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 喀麦隆的 HBV 患病率 总体汇总率为 9.98% (95% CI 9.00–11.02),异质性较高 (I2 = 98.10%)。与相对较低风险人群(8.94%,95% CI 7.84–10.11)相比,患病率 在相对较高风险人群中较高(12.70%,95% CI 10.28–15.32)。亚组分析将性别、地理区域(区域)、人口风险组和研究设计确定为异质性的主要来源。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述报告了显着的异质性(I2 = 98.10%),尽管进行了亚组分析,但在很大程度上仍然无法解释,这表明纳入的研究之间存在潜在的未测量的混杂因素或方法学上的不一致。高度异质性限制了汇总估计的精度,并使区域和人群特定差异的解释变得复杂。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调需针对男性及血清流行率最高的地区实施有针对性的公共卫生干预措施,以减少乙型肝炎病毒传播并改善喀麦隆的防控措施。未来血清流行率研究应采用标准化的研究设计与报告,以减少异质性并提高可比性。

title: Hepatitis B Immunity in Children on Immunomodulators: Implications From a Pediatric Dermatology Cohort and Review of the Literature
abstract: ABSTRACT Background/Objectives This study aims to determine the level of hepatitis B virus (HBV) immunity in patients who had HBV serologic testing prior to starting immunomodulatory medication for dermatologic conditions at a single institution and to review evidence on waning immunity, serologic interpretation, and revaccination. Methods We performed a retrospective chart review of pediatric and young adult patients initiated on immunomodulatory therapy for dermatologic conditions who had HBV serologic testing prior to initiation. A focused literature review was conducted on durability of HBV immunity, HBV serologies in the context of immunomodulatory medications, and revaccination recommendations. Results In this cohort of 23 children, roughly 40% lacked HBV serologic immunity. Prior studies demonstrated that antibody‐mediated protection is heterogeneous and anti‐HBs titers decline over time. Existing guidelines are largely derived from adult populations. Evidence regarding revaccination strategies is mixed. Notably, absence of detectable anti‐HBs antibodies does not always equate to loss of immune memory or susceptibility to infection. Conclusions Anti‐HBs titers are variable and wane over time. Experts agree that patients should receive all recommended vaccinations before starting immunomodulatory therapy and be screened for HBV beforehand, based on adult guidelines. It is uncertain how well these recommendations apply to children, who generally have lower HBV risk and prevalence. Guidance is needed on how to manage pediatric patients without serologic evidence of HBV immunity before beginning biologic treatments.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景/目标 本研究旨在确定在单一机构开始针对皮肤病的免疫调节药物之前进行 HBV 血清学检测的患者的 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 免疫力水平,并审查有关免疫力减弱、血清学解释和重新接种疫苗的证据。方法 我们对因皮肤病而开始接受免疫调节治疗的儿童和年轻成人患者进行了回顾性图表审查,这些患者在开始治疗前进行了 HBV 血清学检测。对 HBV 免疫力的持久性、免疫调节药物背景下的 HBV 血清学以及重新接种建议进行了重点文献综述。结果在23名儿童的队列研究中,大约40%缺乏HBV血清学免疫。先前的研究表明,抗体介导的保护是异质的,并且抗 HBs 滴度随着时间的推移而下降。现有的指南主要来自成年人。关于重新接种策略的证据好坏参半。值得注意的是,缺乏可检测到的抗 HBs 抗体并不总是等同于免疫记忆丧失或对感染的易感性。结论 抗 HBs 滴度是可变的,并且随着时间的推移而减弱。专家们一致认为,患者在开始免疫调节治疗之前应接受所有推荐的 疫苗接种,并根据成人指南事先进行 HBV 筛查。目前尚不确定这些建议对儿童的适用程度如何,因为儿童通常具有较低的 HBV 风险和 患病率。在开始生物制剂 治疗 之前,需要指导如何管理没有 HBV 免疫血清学证据的儿科患者。

title: Prevention, surveillance, and early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma - a Brazilian multidisciplinary consensus.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma is a major cause of cancer-related mortality and represents a growing public health challenge. AIMS: To develop multidisciplinary evidence-based recommendations for the prevention and early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma. METHODS: This consensus was coordinated by the Brazilian Society of Surgical Oncology, with the participation of 13 additional national societies. A steering committee defined the key clinical questions addressing prevention, surveillance, and early detection strategies. Recommendation statements were informed by a comprehensive, non-systematic review of the literature conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library. RESULTS: Eighteen recommendations reached consensus, covering three main domains: 1. Primary prevention, including HBV vaccination, timely antiviral therapy for viral hepatitis, and lifestyle interventions for metabolic dysfunction. Secondary prevention, outlining risk-based surveillance strategies for patients with advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis due to hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Operational standards for surveillance, emphasizing ultrasound as the cornerstone of monitoring, the importance of structured reporting, management of small nodules, and the selective use of cross-sectional imaging. CONCLUSIONS: These multidisciplinary recommendations provide practical, adaptable guidance for the prevention, surveillance, and early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma. This guidance document aims to reduce the burden of hepatocellular carcinoma and support better clinical outcomes across diverse healthcare settings. CENTRAL MESSAGE: Prevention and early detection save lives in liver cancer. This Brazilian multidisciplinary consensus integrates the best scientific evidence and the expertise of specialists from across the country to more effectively guide the prevention, identification, and surveillance of hepatocellular carcinoma. By answering key clinical questions and offering practical, easy-to-use recommendations, this document helps physicians and healthcare teams provide better care to people at risk. PERSPECTIVES: This consensus provides practical guidance to improve the prevention and early detection of liver cancer in daily clinical care. The recommendations emphasize raising awareness of hepatocellular carcinoma, stimulating the development of broader surveillance programs, promoting earlier diagnosis, and improving outcomes for patients at risk for developing primary liver cancer.

title_zh: 预防、监测 和肝细胞癌的早期检测 - 巴西多学科共识。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma is a major cause of cancer-related mortality and represents a growing public health challenge. AIMS: To develop multidisciplinary evidence-based recommendations for the prevention and early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma. METHODS: This consensus was coordinated by the Brazilian Society of Surgical Oncology, with the participation of 13 additional national societies. A steering committee defined the key clinical questions addressing prevention, surveillance, and early detection strategies. Recommendation statements were informed by a comprehensive, non-systematic review of the literature conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library. RESULTS: Eighteen recommendations reached consensus, covering three main domains: 1. Primary prevention, including HBV vaccination, timely antiviral therapy for viral hepatitis, and lifestyle interventions for metabolic dysfunction. Secondary prevention, outlining risk-based surveillance strategies for patients with advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis due to hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Operational standards for surveillance, emphasizing ultrasound as the cornerstone of monitoring, the importance of structured reporting, management of small nodules, and the selective use of cross-sectional imaging. CONCLUSIONS: These multidisciplinary recommendations provide practical, adaptable guidance for the prevention, surveillance, and early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma. This guidance document aims to reduce the burden of hepatocellular carcinoma and support better clinical outcomes across diverse healthcare settings. CENTRAL MESSAGE: Prevention and early detection save lives in liver cancer. This Brazilian multidisciplinary consensus integrates the best scientific evidence and the expertise of specialists from across the country to more effectively guide the prevention, identification, and surveillance of hepatocellular carcinoma. By answering key clinical questions and offering practical, easy-to-use recommendations, this document helps physicians and healthcare teams provide better care to people at risk. PERSPECTIVES: This consensus provides practical guidance to improve the prevention and early detection of liver cancer in daily clinical care. The recommendations emphasize raising awareness of hepatocellular carcinoma, stimulating the development of broader surveillance programs, promoting earlier diagnosis, and improving outcomes for patients at risk for developing primary liver cancer.
abstract_zh: 背景:肝细胞癌是癌症相关 死亡率 的主要原因,也是日益严峻的公共卫生挑战。目的:为预防和早期发现肝细胞癌制定多学科循证建议。方法:该共识由巴西外科肿瘤学会协调,另外 13 个国家学会参与。指导委员会定义了涉及预防、监测 和早期检测策略的关键临床问题。建议声明是通过使用 PubMed、Scopus 和 Cochrane 图书馆对文献进行全面、非系统的审查得出的。结果:18项建议达成共识,涵盖三个主要领域:1.一级预防,包括乙型肝炎疫苗接种、病毒性肝炎的及时抗病毒药物治疗以及代谢功能障碍的生活方式干预。二级预防,概述了针对因 乙型肝炎病毒、丙型肝炎病毒或代谢功能障碍相关的脂肪变性肝病导致的晚期纤维化或肝硬化患者的基于风险的 监测 策略。监测 的操作标准,强调超声作为监测的基石、结构化报告的重要性、小结节的管理以及选择性使用横截面成像。结论:这些多学科建议为肝细胞癌的预防、监测 和早期检测提供了实用、适应性强的指导。本指导文件旨在减轻肝细胞癌的负担,并支持在不同的医疗机构中获得更好的临床结果。中心信息:预防和早期检测可以挽救肝癌的生命。这一巴西多学科共识整合了全国各地专家的最佳科学证据和专业知识,以更有效地指导肝细胞癌的预防、识别和监测。通过回答关键的临床问题并提供实用、易于使用的建议,本文档帮助医生和医疗团队为高危人群提供更好的护理。观点:本共识为改善日常临床护理中肝癌的预防和早期发现提供了实用指导。这些建议强调提高对肝细胞癌的认识,刺激更广泛的 监测 项目的开发,促进早期 诊断 的发展,并改善有原发性肝癌风险的患者的预后。

title: Serologic Immunity to Hepatitis A and B in US Adults and High-Risk Populations
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Serologic immunity to hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) protects against acute infection and severe outcomes among high-risk groups; however, contemporary data on population-level immunity remain limited, especially in high-risk populations. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence and factors associated with serologic immunity in the overall population and across high-risk subgroups, including those with chronic liver disease (CLD), chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and immunosuppression and pregnant people. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from January 2017 to August 2023 and included adults aged 20 years or older with available HAV and HBV serologic test results. Data were analyzed from January 3 to May 10, 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were the prevalence of serologic immunity to HAV, defined by hepatitis A antibody positivity, and HBV, defined by hepatitis B surface antibody positivity, with vaccine-derived immunity specifically identified by surface antibody positivity in the absence of hepatitis B core antibodies. Data were weighted to generate nationally representative estimates of the US adult population. Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression models were used to identify independent factors associated with viral hepatitis immunity. RESULTS: Among 13 514 individuals, representing an estimated 226.1 million US adults (mean [SE] age, 48.65 [0.40] years; 51.76% female), 39.5% (95% CI, 37.7%-41.3%) demonstrated serologic immunity to hepatitis A, corresponding to approximately 89.4 million individuals. For HBV, 27.1% (95% CI, 25.8%-28.4%) demonstrated serologic immunity, corresponding to approximately 61.3 million individuals, while vaccine-derived immunity was present in 25.2% (95% CI, 23.9%-26.5%). In adjusted models, HAV immunity was associated with younger age (eg, 20-29 vs ≥65 years: adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 0.51; 95% CI, 0.44-0.60); lower educational attainment (eg, <grade 9 vs college graduate or above: AOR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.24-0.42); non-Hispanic Black (AOR, 1.67; 95% CI, 1.34-2.09), Mexican American (AOR, 4.22; 95% CI, 3.42-5.21), other Hispanic (AOR, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.60-2.54), non-Hispanic Asian (AOR, 3.03; 95% CI, 2.45-3.76), and multiracial or other (AOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.04-1.79) race and ethnicity; being born outside the US (AOR, 4.54; 95% CI, 3.74-5.52); and liver disease awareness (OR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.29-2.09). Obesity was associated with lower odds of HAV immunity (AOR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.72-0.96). Vaccine-derived HBV immunity was associated with younger age (eg, 20-29 vs ≥65 years: AOR, 0.18; 95% CI, 0.15-0.23), female sex (AOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.18-1.56), non-Hispanic Asian (AOR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.17-1.86) and non-Hispanic Black (AOR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.00-1.32) race and ethnicity, and higher educational attainment (eg, <grade 9 vs college graduate or above: AOR, 3.29; 95% CI, 2.35-4.61). In high-risk subgroups, HAV immunity ranged from 26.7% (95% CI, 18.9%-34.4%) for metabolic dysfunction-associated alcohol-related liver disease to 63.7% (95% CI, 50.0%-77.4%) for chronic HBV infection, while HBV vaccine-derived immunity ranged from 14.0% (95% CI, 11.3%-16.6%) for chronic kidney disease to 38.6% (95% CI, 28.0%-49.1%) for pregnancy. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cross-sectional study found that population-level serologic immunity to HAV and HBV was suboptimal and substantial susceptibility persisted across high-risk clinical subgroups. These findings highlight persistent gaps in viral hepatitis protection and support targeted, systematic vaccination strategies for HAV and HBV, especially among high-risk populations.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in US adults, focusing on serologic immunity prevalence and factors associated with vaccine-derived HBV immunity, specifically targeting adults aged 20 years or older and high-risk subgroups such as those with chronic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, immunosuppression, and pregnancy (A2, A5).

Data were analyzed from January 3 to May 10, 2026, and weighted to generate nationally representative estimates (A4, A6). Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression models identified independent factors associated with HBV immunity (A7).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that population-level serologic immunity to HBV was suboptimal, with 27.1% (95% CI, 25.8%-28.4%) demonstrating serologic immunity and 25.2% (95% CI, 23.9%-26.5%) exhibiting vaccine-derived immunity, corresponding to approximately 61.3 million and 56.9 million individuals, respectively (A9). analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights substantial susceptibility to HBV across high-risk clinical subgroups, with vaccine-derived immunity ranging from 14.0% (95% CI, 11.3%-16.6%) in chronic kidney disease to 38.6% (95% CI, 28.0%-49.1%) in pregnancy, indicating persistent gaps in protection despite vaccination efforts (A13).
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for targeted, systematic vaccination strategies for HBV, particularly among high-risk populations, to address suboptimal immunity and reduce susceptibility (A15).

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates serologic immunity to hepatitis B virus (HBV) in US adults using NHANES data from 2017 to 2023. It reports that only 27.1% of adults demonstrate serologic immunity to HBV, with vaccine-derived immunity present in 25.2%, translating to approximately 61.3 million and 56.9 million individuals, respectively. Vaccine-derived immunity is more prevalent among younger adults, females, non-Hispanic Asian and Black individuals, and those with higher education. However, immunity remains suboptimal across high-risk subgroups, including chronic kidney disease (14.0%) and pregnancy (38.6%). The findings underscore persistent gaps in HBV protection and support the implementation of targeted vaccination strategies to improve immunity, particularly in high-risk populations.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that population-level serologic immunity to HBV was suboptimal, with 27.1% (95% CI, 25.8%-28.4%) demonstrating serologic immunity and 25.2% (95% CI, 23.9%-26.5%) exhibiting vaccine-derived immunity, corresponding to approximately 61.3 million and 56.9 million individuals, respectively (A9). Vaccine-derived HBV immunity was associated with younger age, female sex, non-Hispanic Asian and non-Hispanic Black race and ethnicity, and higher educational attainment (A12).
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights substantial susceptibility to HBV across high-risk clinical subgroups, with vaccine-derived immunity ranging from 14.0% (95% CI, 11.3%-16.6%) in chronic kidney disease to 38.6% (95% CI, 28.0%-49.1%) in pregnancy, indicating persistent gaps in protection despite vaccination efforts (A13).
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要针对乙肝病毒(特别是高危人群)制定有针对性的、系统的 疫苗接种 策略,以解决免疫力不佳的问题并降低易感性 (A15)。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in US adults, focusing on serologic immunity prevalence and factors associated with vaccine-derived HBV immunity, specifically targeting adults aged 20 years or older and high-risk subgroups such as those with chronic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, immunosuppression, and pregnancy (A2, A5).
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review uses a cross-sectional design with data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from January 2017 to August 2023, including 13,514 adults with available HBV serologic test results (A3). Data were analyzed from January 3 to May 10, 2026, and weighted to generate nationally representative estimates (A4, A6). Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression models identified independent factors associated with HBV immunity (A7).
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that population-level serologic immunity to HBV was suboptimal, with 27.1% (95% CI, 25.8%-28.4%) demonstrating serologic immunity and 25.2% (95% CI, 23.9%-26.5%) exhibiting vaccine-derived immunity, corresponding to approximately 61.3 million and 56.9 million individuals, respectively (A9). Vaccine-derived HBV immunity was associated with younger age, female sex, non-Hispanic Asian and non-Hispanic Black race and ethnicity, and higher educational attainment (A12).
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights substantial susceptibility to HBV across high-risk clinical subgroups, with vaccine-derived immunity ranging from 14.0% (95% CI, 11.3%-16.6%) in chronic kidney disease to 38.6% (95% CI, 28.0%-49.1%) in pregnancy, indicating persistent gaps in protection despite vaccination efforts (A13).
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for targeted, systematic vaccination strategies for HBV, particularly among high-risk populations, to address suboptimal immunity and reduce susceptibility (A15).

title_zh: 美国成人和高危人群对甲型和乙型肝炎的血清学免疫
source_body_en: IMPORTANCE: Serologic immunity to hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) protects against acute infection and severe outcomes among high-risk groups; however, contemporary data on population-level immunity remain limited, especially in high-risk populations. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence and factors associated with serologic immunity in the overall population and across high-risk subgroups, including those with chronic liver disease (CLD), chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and immunosuppression and pregnant people. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from January 2017 to August 2023 and included adults aged 20 years or older with available HAV and HBV serologic test results. Data were analyzed from January 3 to May 10, 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were the prevalence of serologic immunity to HAV, defined by hepatitis A antibody positivity, and HBV, defined by hepatitis B surface antibody positivity, with vaccine-derived immunity specifically identified by surface antibody positivity in the absence of hepatitis B core antibodies. Data were weighted to generate nationally representative estimates of the US adult population. Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression models were used to identify independent factors associated with viral hepatitis immunity. RESULTS: Among 13 514 individuals, representing an estimated 226.1 million US adults (mean [SE] age, 48.65 [0.40] years; 51.76% female), 39.5% (95% CI, 37.7%-41.3%) demonstrated serologic immunity to hepatitis A, corresponding to approximately 89.4 million individuals. For HBV, 27.1% (95% CI, 25.8%-28.4%) demonstrated serologic immunity, corresponding to approximately 61.3 million individuals, while vaccine-derived immunity was present in 25.2% (95% CI, 23.9%-26.5%). In adjusted models, HAV immunity was associated with younger age (eg, 20-29 vs ≥65 years: adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 0.51; 95% CI, 0.44-0.60); lower educational attainment (eg, <grade 9 vs college graduate or above: AOR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.24-0.42); non-Hispanic Black (AOR, 1.67; 95% CI, 1.34-2.09), Mexican American (AOR, 4.22; 95% CI, 3.42-5.21), other Hispanic (AOR, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.60-2.54), non-Hispanic Asian (AOR, 3.03; 95% CI, 2.45-3.76), and multiracial or other (AOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.04-1.79) race and ethnicity; being born outside the US (AOR, 4.54; 95% CI, 3.74-5.52); and liver disease awareness (OR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.29-2.09). Obesity was associated with lower odds of HAV immunity (AOR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.72-0.96). Vaccine-derived HBV immunity was associated with younger age (eg, 20-29 vs ≥65 years: AOR, 0.18; 95% CI, 0.15-0.23), female sex (AOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.18-1.56), non-Hispanic Asian (AOR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.17-1.86) and non-Hispanic Black (AOR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.00-1.32) race and ethnicity, and higher educational attainment (eg, <grade 9 vs college graduate or above: AOR, 3.29; 95% CI, 2.35-4.61). In high-risk subgroups, HAV immunity ranged from 26.7% (95% CI, 18.9%-34.4%) for metabolic dysfunction-associated alcohol-related liver disease to 63.7% (95% CI, 50.0%-77.4%) for chronic HBV infection, while HBV vaccine-derived immunity ranged from 14.0% (95% CI, 11.3%-16.6%) for chronic kidney disease to 38.6% (95% CI, 28.0%-49.1%) for pregnancy. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cross-sectional study found that population-level serologic immunity to HAV and HBV was suboptimal and substantial susceptibility persisted across high-risk clinical subgroups. These findings highlight persistent gaps in viral hepatitis protection and support targeted, systematic vaccination strategies for HAV and HBV, especially among high-risk populations.

title: Hepatitis B and C Prevention, Screening, and Diagnostic Services at HIV Treatment Sites: International Epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prevention, screening, and diagnostic services for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) can prevent morbidity and mortality in people receiving HIV care. However, there is limited information about the availability of HBV and HCV services at HIV clinics globally. METHODS: The International epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA) conducted surveys of service delivery and practices at participating HIV treatment centers from 7 regions. We used 2023 survey data to measure availability of HBV vaccination, HBV and HCV screening, HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to test associations of site characteristics with HBV and HCV services. RESULTS: HBV vaccination was available on-site at 67.7% of 204 HIV treatment sites. Screening for HBV and HCV at HIV care enrollment was reported by 72.1% and 50% of sites, respectively. HBsAg, HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing were available on-site at 77%, 47.6%, 61.8%, and 44.6% of sites, respectively. Sites serving predominately rural (vs. urban) populations were less likely to report on-site availability of HBV DNA [odds ratio (OR):0.07; 95% confidence interval: 0.01 to 0.68; P = 0.02], HCV antibody (OR = 0.18; 95% CI: 0.04 to 0.92; P = 0.04), and HCV RNA (OR = 0.10; 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.90; P = 0.04) testing. CONCLUSION: Life-saving services such as HBV vaccination, HBsAg, and HCV antibody testing were available on-site at most HIV treatment sites participating in the IeDEA network. Lower availability at rural sites suggests that expansion of services is important to eliminate HBV and HCV as public health problems in people receiving HIV care.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health problem that morbidity and mortality from hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) remain high among people receiving HIV care, despite the availability of effective prevention and diagnostic services. The authors identified a knowledge gap regarding the global availability of HBV and HCV services at HIV clinics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The International epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA) conducted a cross-sectional survey of service delivery and practices at 204 HIV treatment centers across seven global regions in 2023.
analysis.methods: The survey measured on-site availability of HBV vaccination, HBV and HCV screening, and specific tests (HBsAg, HBV DNA, HCV antibody, HCV RNA). Multivariable logistic regression models were used to test associations between site characteristics and the availability of HBV and HCV services.
analysis.main_results: HBV vaccination was available on-site at 67.7% of sites, screening for HBV and HCV at enrollment was reported by 72.1% and 50% of sites, respectively, and HBsAg, HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing were available on-site at 77%, 47.6%, 61.8%, and 44.6% of sites, respectively. Sites serving predominantly rural populations were less likely to offer on-site HBV DNA (OR 0.07; 95% CI 0.01–0.68; P=0.02), HCV antibody (OR 0.18; 95% CI 0.04–0.92; P=0.04), and HCV RNA (OR 0.10; 95% CI 0.01–0.90; P=0.04) testing.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that life-saving HBV and HCV services were available on-site at most participating HIV treatment sites, but lower availability in rural settings highlights a service gap that could impede elimination efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that expanding HBV and HCV services, particularly in rural areas, is critical to achieving elimination goals among people receiving HIV care.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported survey data limit causal inference and may overestimate service availability; the evidence strength is moderate due to potential reporting bias and limited generalizability beyond IeDEA network sites.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional survey within the International epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA) assessed the availability of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) prevention and diagnostic services at 204 HIV treatment centers across seven global regions in 2023. The study found that HBV vaccination was available on-site at 67.7% of sites, screening for HBV and HCV at enrollment was reported by 72.1% and 50% of sites, respectively, and HBsAg, HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing were available on-site at 77%, 47.6%, 61.8%, and 44.6% of sites, respectively. Sites serving predominantly rural populations were significantly less likely to offer HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing. The authors concluded that while life-saving HBV and HCV services were available at most participating sites, lower availability in rural settings indicates a need for targeted expansion to support elimination goals among people receiving HIV care.

elements_en.main_results: HBV vaccination was available on-site at 67.7% of sites, screening for HBV and HCV at enrollment was reported by 72.1% and 50% of sites, respectively, and HBsAg, HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing were available on-site at 77%, 47.6%, 61.8%, and 44.6% of sites, respectively. elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that life-saving HBV and HCV services were available on-site at most participating HIV treatment sites, but lower availability in rural settings highlights a service gap that could impede elimination efforts.

title_zh: HIV 治疗 网站的乙型和丙型肝炎预防、筛查和诊断服务:评估艾滋病的国际 流行病学 数据库。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Prevention, screening, and diagnostic services for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) can prevent morbidity and mortality in people receiving HIV care. However, there is limited information about the availability of HBV and HCV services at HIV clinics globally. METHODS: The International epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA) conducted surveys of service delivery and practices at participating HIV treatment centers from 7 regions. We used 2023 survey data to measure availability of HBV vaccination, HBV and HCV screening, HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to test associations of site characteristics with HBV and HCV services. RESULTS: HBV vaccination was available on-site at 67.7% of 204 HIV treatment sites. Screening for HBV and HCV at HIV care enrollment was reported by 72.1% and 50% of sites, respectively. HBsAg, HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing were available on-site at 77%, 47.6%, 61.8%, and 44.6% of sites, respectively. Sites serving predominately rural (vs. urban) populations were less likely to report on-site availability of HBV DNA [odds ratio (OR):0.07; 95% confidence interval: 0.01 to 0.68; P = 0.02], HCV antibody (OR = 0.18; 95% CI: 0.04 to 0.92; P = 0.04), and HCV RNA (OR = 0.10; 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.90; P = 0.04) testing. CONCLUSION: Life-saving services such as HBV vaccination, HBsAg, and HCV antibody testing were available on-site at most HIV treatment sites participating in the IeDEA network. Lower availability at rural sites suggests that expansion of services is important to eliminate HBV and HCV as public health problems in people receiving HIV care.

title: Barriers to Hepatitis B Treatment: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Registry and Survey Study by the Canadian Hepatitis B Network.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide, yet treatment uptake is suboptimal even in high-resource settings. This pan-Canadian study aimed to quantify treatment gaps within the Canadian Hepatitis B Network (CanHepB) Registry, compare characteristics of treatment-eligible but untreated patients to those receiving therapy, and assess patient and specialist perspectives on barriers to treatment. METHODS: A cross-sectional, retrospective analysis of 1983 adults with CHB followed in 18 Canadian hepatitis B specialty clinics between January 2018 and November 2024. Treatment eligibility was determined using the 2018 Canadian Association for the Study of the Liver guidelines. An anonymous survey captured patient-reported barriers and perspectives (n = 191), while a separate survey evaluated specialist perceptions (n = 54). RESULTS: Among 881 untreated patients, 46.4% (n = 409) were treatment eligible. Compared with the treatment group (n = 1087), the treatment-eligible but untreated patients were younger (median 47.3 vs. 54.5 years), more frequently female (54.2% vs. 39.7%), and more likely to be of Black/African/Caribbean origin (18.2% vs. They had a lower prevalence of cirrhosis (2.4% vs. 20.3%), HCC (0.7% vs. 9.3%), and hypertension (17.1% vs. 22.9%), but a higher prevalence of steatotic liver disease (36.4% vs. 24.6%) and dyslipidemia (14.7% vs. Among untreated respondents, concerns included side effects, the need for long-term therapy, and lack of curative options. Conversely, specialists identified cost as the primary barrier and side effects as the least concerning. CONCLUSION: This nationwide study reveals a significant treatment gap in CHB care, driven by demographic disparities and a mismatch between patient concerns and clinician perceptions.

title: Clinical progress note: Hepatitis B
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B virus is a well‐known infectious etiology of acute and chronic liver disease worldwide. Notably, 90% of children infected with hepatitis B in infancy develop chronic infection and subsequent progressive liver disease, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Significant reduction in perinatal transmission in the United States (US) was seen after implementation of universal infant vaccination 30 years ago, as well as dramatic reductions in HBV incidence across Asia, coinciding with widespread hepatitis B vaccination. However, with ongoing changes to federal vaccine guidance and a steady rise in vaccine hesitancy, a comprehensive understanding of the epidemiology, transmission, screening, and prevention of hepatitis B remains important for pediatric health care providers.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一份临床进展报告,重点关注人类 乙型肝炎病毒 感染,特别是在儿科医疗保健方面。它讨论了 疫苗接种 计划的影响以及联邦 疫苗 指南的变化和 疫苗 犹豫所带来的持续挑战。
elements_zh.methods: 所提供的证据中没有明确详细说明方法部分,但该研究参考了美国通用婴儿 传播 的实施及其对减少 传播 围产期 传播 的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究报告称,自 30 年前实施通用婴儿 传播 以来,美国围产期 传播 显着减少。它还注意到整个亚洲的 HBV 发病率 急剧减少,与广泛传播的乙型肝炎 发病率 一致。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,疫苗接种 计划的成功导致了 乙型肝炎病毒 的 传播 和 发病率 的减少,但他们强调,由于 疫苗 指南的不断变化和犹豫不决,需要全面了解其 流行病学 和预防措施。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明了维持 疫苗接种 计划和了解 乙型肝炎病毒 的 流行病学 的重要性,以应对持续的公共卫生挑战,特别是在儿科人群中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究没有提供详细的方法或统计分析,其结论是基于观察数据而不是对照实验。由于缺乏具体的统计细节,证据的强度中等。

title: Attendance Among People With Hepatitis B in UK Secondary Care: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Chronic Hepatitis B disease requires lifelong monitoring to prevent complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite structured care pathways, non-attendance within UK secondary care remains challenging. This scoping review aimed to synthesise existing evidence on factors influencing non-attendance at secondary care appointments and strategies to improve appointment adherence among people living with Chronic Hepatitis B. Eligibility Criteria: Peer-reviewed sources examining adults with Hepatitis B attendance at UK secondary care services. Grey literature was excluded. Sources of Evidence: Searches were performed in CINAHL Ultimate, Medline, Embase, Scopus and APA PsycINFO. Data were charted using a structured data extraction form and synthesised narratively. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria. Identified barriers included patient-related factors (e.g., limited health literacy, stigmatisation, competing priorities), system-level challenges (e.g., appointment scheduling and accessibility) and cultural or language barriers. Psychological factors, including fear of diagnosis and treatment side effects, were also reported. Reported strategies included patient education, culturally tailored interventions, reminder systems (e.g., SMS and telephone calls) and integrated care models involving community outreach. Non-attendance among people with chronic Hepatitis B in secondary care is influenced by a complex interplay of personal, social and systemic factors. Interventions that address multiple barriers, particularly those that incorporate culturally sensitive approaches and reminder systems, may improve engagement. Further research is needed to co-design and evaluate interventions with affected communities.

title: Higher Off-Therapy Relapse Risk with Tenofovir Alafenamide than Entecavir in Non-cirrhotic HBeAg-Negative Chronic Hepatitis B: Insights from End-of-Treatment qHBsAg Stratification
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: End-of-treatment (EOT) qHBsAg predicts off-therapy relapse in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B (CHB), but whether its stratifying ability differs between entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) remains unclear. This study compared 12-month relapse risk across EOT qHBsAg strata after ETV or TAF discontinuation in non-cirrhotic HBeAg-negative CHB patients. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, non-cirrhotic HBeAg-negative CHB patients discontinuing ETV or TAF were 1:1 propensity score matched. Virological relapse was assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression; clinical relapse by cumulative incidence functions with Fine-Gray competing risks regression. Hazard ratios and subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) were compared across EOT qHBsAg strata (< 2, 2-3, ≥3 log10 IU/mL). RESULTS: A total of 130 patients (65 per group) were analyzed. Among ETV discontinuers, clinical relapse rates increased progressively with higher EOT qHBsAg (0.0%, 14.6%, and 25.0% for <2, 2-3, and ≥3 log10 IU/mL, respectively). In contrast, TAF discontinuers showed persistently high virological (68.8%-86.3%) and clinical relapse rates (48.5%-57.1%) regardless of EOT qHBsAg level. The relapse risk difference was most pronounced at lower EOT qHBsAg: the sHR for clinical relapse (TAF vs. ETV) reached 5.164 (95% CI 2.131-12.515) at 2-3 log10 IU/mL, with no ETV events at <2 log10 IU/mL. Overall sHR was 5.633 (95% CI 2.801-11.329; p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: EOT qHBsAg effectively stratifies clinical relapse risk after ETV discontinuation but shows limited discriminative ability after TAF cessation, where relapse rates remain uniformly high across all qHBsAg levels.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective design, modest sample size (n=130), and single-centre setting limit generalisability and may introduce selection bias; the evidence is assessed as moderate due to these constraints and the absence of external validation.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study compared off-therapy relapse risk after discontinuation of entecavir (ETV) versus tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in 130 non-cirrhotic HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients matched 1:1 by propensity score. title_zh: 在非肝硬化 HBeAg 阴性 慢性乙型肝炎 中,替诺福韦艾拉酚胺的治疗后复发风险高于恩替卡韦:治疗 结束时 qHBsAg 分层的见解
source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: End-of-treatment (EOT) qHBsAg predicts off-therapy relapse in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B (CHB), but whether its stratifying ability differs between entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) remains unclear. This study compared 12-month relapse risk across EOT qHBsAg strata after ETV or TAF discontinuation in non-cirrhotic HBeAg-negative CHB patients. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, non-cirrhotic HBeAg-negative CHB patients discontinuing ETV or TAF were 1:1 propensity score matched. Virological relapse was assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression; clinical relapse by cumulative incidence functions with Fine-Gray competing risks regression. Hazard ratios and subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) were compared across EOT qHBsAg strata (< 2, 2-3, ≥3 log10 IU/mL). RESULTS: A total of 130 patients (65 per group) were analyzed. Among ETV discontinuers, clinical relapse rates increased progressively with higher EOT qHBsAg (0.0%, 14.6%, and 25.0% for <2, 2-3, and ≥3 log10 IU/mL, respectively). In contrast, TAF discontinuers showed persistently high virological (68.8%-86.3%) and clinical relapse rates (48.5%-57.1%) regardless of EOT qHBsAg level. The relapse risk difference was most pronounced at lower EOT qHBsAg: the sHR for clinical relapse (TAF vs. ETV) reached 5.164 (95% CI 2.131-12.515) at 2-3 log10 IU/mL, with no ETV events at <2 log10 IU/mL. Overall sHR was 5.633 (95% CI 2.801-11.329; p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: EOT qHBsAg effectively stratifies clinical relapse risk after ETV discontinuation but shows limited discriminative ability after TAF cessation, where relapse rates remain uniformly high across all qHBsAg levels.

title: Hepatic Artery Doppler Haemodynamic Indices as Imaging Biomarkers of Disease Activity in Adults with Chronic Hepatitis B: Correlation with Viral Load and Serum Alanine Transaminase
abstract: Abstract Background: Hepatitis B is a common cause of chronic liver disease. Early features of fibrosis are detectable using ultrasound and Doppler imaging. Aims: This study evaluated relationships between hepatic artery Doppler parameters, serum alanine transaminase (ALT) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) quantification (viral load) in seropositive adults with hepatitis B compared with matched healthy controls. Materials and Methods: A comparative cross-sectional study assessed grayscale liver ultrasound, hepatic artery Doppler indices, ALT and viral load among 143 asymptomatic hepatitis B-positive adults and matched controls. Liver size, echotexture, resistive index (RI), pulsatility index (PI), ALT and HBV DNA levels were measured. Data were summarised using mean, median and standard deviation. Chi-square and t -tests compared groups, while Pearson correlation assessed relationships among ALT, RI and PI, with significance at P < 0.05. Results: The study compared 143 chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients with 143 healthy controls. No significant differences were observed in liver span (13.0 vs. 12.8 cm) or echogenicity, but hepatic artery Doppler indices were significantly elevated in hepatitis B patients (0.69 vs. 0.61 for RI and 1.25 vs. Elevated ALT levels and detectable viral loads were more common in patients on treatment. Doppler indices correlated significantly with ALT and the viral load, suggesting their potential role in monitoring hepatitis B progression. Conclusion: Doppler ultrasound remains a valuable non-invasive tool for assessing hepatic vascular changes among asymptomatic CHB-positive patients with RI and PI revealing those changes. Doppler indices correlated significantly with abnormal serum ALT and elevated viral load levels among hepatitis B-positive patients.

Aims: This study evaluated relationships between hepatic artery Doppler parameters, serum alanine transaminase (ALT) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) quantification (viral load) in seropositive adults with hepatitis B compared with matched healthy controls. Materials and Methods: A comparative cross-sectional study assessed grayscale liver ultrasound, hepatic artery Doppler indices, ALT and viral load among 143 asymptomatic hepatitis B-positive adults and matched controls. Liver size, echotexture, resistive index (RI), pulsatility index (PI), ALT and HBV DNA levels were measured. Data were summarised using mean, median and standard deviation. Chi-square and t -tests compared groups, while Pearson correlation assessed relationships among ALT, RI and PI, with significance at P < 0.05. Results: The study compared 143 chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients with 143 healthy controls. No significant differences were observed in liver span (13.0 vs. 12.8 cm) or echogenicity, but hepatic artery Doppler indices were significantly elevated in hepatitis B patients (0.69 vs. 0.61 for RI and 1.25 vs. Elevated ALT levels and detectable viral loads were more common in patients on treatment. Doppler indices correlated significantly with ALT and the viral load, suggesting their potential role in monitoring hepatitis B progression. Conclusion: Doppler ultrasound remains a valuable non-invasive tool for assessing hepatic vascular changes among asymptomatic CHB-positive patients with RI and PI revealing those changes. Doppler indices correlated significantly with abnormal serum ALT and elevated viral load levels among hepatitis B-positive patients.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relationship between hepatic artery Doppler parameters, serum ALT levels, and HBV DNA quantification in asymptomatic adults with chronic hepatitis B compared to healthy controls. The research aimed to explore the potential of Doppler imaging as a non-invasive biomarker for disease activity. A comparative cross-sectional design was used, involving 143 patients and 143 controls. Doppler indices, including resistive index (RI) and pulsatility index (PI), were measured alongside ALT and viral load. Results showed no significant differences in liver span or echogenicity, but Doppler indices were significantly elevated in hepatitis B patients. These indices correlated with abnormal ALT and elevated viral load, suggesting their utility in monitoring disease progression. The findings highlight the potential of Doppler ultrasound as a tool for assessing hepatic vascular changes in CHB. However, the study's cross-sectional nature and reliance on abstract-only data limit the strength of the evidence, indicating moderate confidence in the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估乙型肝炎血清阳性成人与匹配的健康对照者的肝动脉多普勒参数、血清丙氨酸转氨酶 (ALT) 和 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) DNA 定量之间的关系。乙型肝炎是慢性肝病的常见原因,纤维化的早期特征可以通过超声和​​多普勒成像来检测。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项比较横断面研究评估了 143 名无症状乙型肝炎阳性成人和匹配对照者的灰度肝脏超声、肝动脉多普勒指数、ALT 和病毒载量。该研究将 143 名 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者与 143 名健康对照者进行了比较。
elements_zh.methods: 测量肝脏大小、回声纹理、阻力指数 (RI)、搏动指数 (PI)、ALT 和 HBV DNA 水平。使用平均值、中位数和标准差来总结数据。卡方和 t 检验比较各组,而 Pearson 相关性评估 ALT、RI 和 PI 之间的关系,显着性为 P < 0.05。
elements_zh.main_results: 肝跨度(13.0 厘米与 12.8 厘米)或回声性没有观察到显着差异,但乙型肝炎患者的肝动脉多普勒指数显着升高(RI 为 0.69 与 0.61,RI 为 1.25 与 1.25)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 多普勒指数与乙型肝炎阳性患者血清 ALT 异常和病毒载量水平升高显着相关,表明其在监测乙型肝炎进展方面具有潜在作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 服用 治疗 的患者中 ALT 水平升高和可检测到的病毒载量更常见,这表明监测这些参数对于疾病管理的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其横断面设计和对仅摘要证据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。由于缺乏长期随访和详细的临床结果,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 摘要背景:乙型肝炎是慢性肝病的常见原因。使用超声和多普勒成像可以检测纤维化的早期特征。目的:本研究评估了乙型肝炎血清阳性成人与匹配的健康对照者的肝动脉多普勒参数、血清丙氨酸转氨酶 (ALT) 和 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 脱氧核糖核酸 (DNA) 定量(病毒载量)之间的关系。材料和方法:一项比较横断面研究评估了 143 名无症状乙型肝炎阳性成人和匹配对照者的灰度肝脏超声、肝动脉多普勒指数、ALT 和病毒载量。测量肝脏大小、回声纹理、阻力指数 (RI)、搏动指数 (PI)、ALT 和 HBV DNA 水平。使用平均值、中位数和标准差来总结数据。卡方和 t 检验比较各组,而 Pearson 相关性评估 ALT、RI 和 PI 之间的关系,显着性为 P < 0.05。结果:该研究将 143 名 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者与 143 名健康对照者进行了比较。肝跨度(13.0 厘米与 12.8 厘米)或回声性没有观察到显着差异,但乙型肝炎患者的肝动脉多普勒指数显着升高(RI 为 0.69 与 0.61,RI 为 1.25 与 1.25)。治疗 患者中 ALT 水平和可检测到的病毒载量升高更为常见。多普勒指数与 ALT 和病毒载量显着相关,表明它们在监测乙型肝炎进展方面具有潜在作用。结论:多普勒超声仍然是评估无症状 CHB 阳性患者肝血管变化的有价值的非侵入性工具,其 RI 和 PI 揭示了这些变化与乙型肝炎阳性患者血清 ALT 异常和病毒载量水平升高显着相关。

title: Hepatitis B and hepatitis C awareness, knowledge, and practices among adults in the Kyrgyz Republic—results from a nationally representative survey, 2024
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B and hepatitis C are primary drivers of cirrhosis, a leading cause of death in the Kyrgyz Republic (KR). Assessing hepatitis B and hepatitis C awareness, knowledge, and behavioral practices are important to guide prevention, testing, and education interventions. Methods During June–September 2024, we conducted a cross-sectional survey using a stratified multi-stage cluster sampling targeting 6090 adults in KR. We administered a questionnaire through face-to-face interviews to assess hepatitis B and hepatitis C awareness, knowledge, practices (testing and vaccination), and sources of health information. Among respondents aware of hepatitis B and/or hepatitis C, we assessed overall knowledge and factors associated with low knowledge (defined as ≤ 11/17 questions answered correctly for hepatitis B and ≤ 12/18 questions answered correctly for hepatitis C, with each correct response scored as 1). We performed multivariable regression to identify sociodemographic factors and practices associated with hepatitis B and hepatitis C awareness and knowledge. Results Of 6090 targeted adults, 5243 completed the interview. Overall, 43.7% had heard of hepatitis B and 29.2% had heard of hepatitis C. Overall, 28.6% and 25.4% had ever been tested for hepatitis B or hepatitis C, respectively, and 11.6% had been vaccinated against hepatitis B. Among participants aware of hepatitis B or hepatitis C, 24.6% and 28.2% correctly answered all transmission questions, and 19.4% and 4.2% correctly answered all prevention questions, respectively. Female sex, post-secondary education compared to secondary education, and prior hepatitis C testing were all positively associated with hepatitis B and hepatitis C awareness and related knowledge. Factors associated with low knowledge score for hepatitis B included male sex, age 50–59 years (compared to 18–29 years), and being a homemaker. Factors associated with low hepatitis C knowledge were male sex, being a homemaker, and no prior hepatitis C testing ( P -value < 0.05). Internet was the most common source of trusted health information (87.4%). Conclusions The study demonstrated the need to improve levels of hepatitis B and hepatitis C awareness and knowledge, and testing and vaccination uptake. Education programs tailored to reach specific sociodemographic groups are needed to achieve hepatitis B and hepatitis C elimination in KR.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adults in the Kyrgyz Republic, focusing on awareness, knowledge, and practices (testing and vaccination) as drivers of HBV-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The central question addresses the levels of HBV awareness and knowledge and associated sociodemographic factors influencing these outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review reports a cross-sectional survey conducted from June to September 2024 using stratified multi-stage cluster sampling targeting 6090 adults in the Kyrgyz Republic. A face-to-face questionnaire assessed HBV awareness, knowledge, testing, vaccination, and sources of health information. Multivariable regression identified sociodemographic factors and practices associated with HBV awareness and knowledge.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HBV awareness (43.7%) and knowledge levels are low among adults in the Kyrgyz Republic. Only 28.6% had ever been tested for HBV, and 11.6% had been vaccinated against HBV. Female sex, post-secondary education, and prior HCV testing were positively associated with HBV awareness and knowledge, while male sex, age 50–59 years, and being a homemaker were associated with lower HBV knowledge scores.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights significant gaps in HBV awareness (43.7%) and knowledge, with only 19.4% correctly answering all HBV prevention questions. Internet was the most common source of trusted health information (87.4%), but its role in improving HBV-specific knowledge remains unclear. The study does not address HBV genotypes or virological characteristics, limiting insights into transmission dynamics or disease severity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for targeted education programs to improve HBV awareness and knowledge, particularly among males, older adults (50–59 years), and homemakers. It also underscores the importance of increasing HBV testing and vaccination uptake, with internet-based interventions potentially leveraging the high reliance on online health information sources.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates hepatitis B virus (HBV) awareness, knowledge, and practices among adults in the Kyrgyz Republic using a nationally representative cross-sectional survey conducted in 2024. Among 6090 targeted adults, 5243 completed interviews, revealing low HBV awareness (43.7%) and knowledge, with only 28.6% ever tested and 11.6% vaccinated. Female sex, higher education, and prior hepatitis C testing were associated with better HBV awareness and knowledge, while male sex, age 50–59 years, and being a homemaker correlated with lower knowledge scores. Internet was the dominant source of trusted health information (87.4%), suggesting potential for digital interventions. Key gaps include low HBV knowledge (19.4% correctly answered prevention questions) and lack of genotype-specific data. Priorities include tailored education programs for high-risk groups and strategies to enhance testing and vaccination uptake.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述调查了吉尔吉斯共和国成人中的人类 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染,重点关注作为 HBV 相关肝硬化和肝细胞癌驱动因素的认识、知识和实践(测试和 疫苗接种)。核心问题涉及乙型肝炎的认识和知识水平以及影响这些结果的相关社会人口因素。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查报告了 2024 年 6 月至 9 月针对吉尔吉斯共和国 6090 名成年人进行的分层多阶段整群抽样的横断面调查。面对面的调查问卷评估了乙肝病毒的认知、知识、检测、疫苗接种 和健康信息来源。多变量回归确定了与乙型肝炎意识和知识相关的社会人口因素和实践。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,吉尔吉斯斯坦共和国成年人对乙肝病毒的认识(43.7%)和知识水平较低。只有 28.6% 的人曾经接受过 HBV 检测,11.6% 的人接种过 HBV 疫苗。女性、高等教育和既往 HCV 检测与 HBV 认知和知识呈正相关,而男性、年龄 50-59 岁以及家庭主妇与较低的 HBV 知识得分相关。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查突显了人们对 HBV 认识 (43.7%) 和知识的显着差距,只有 19.4% 的人正确回答了所有 HBV 预防问题。互联网是最常见的可信健康信息来源 (87.4%),但其在提高 HBV 特异性知识方面的作用仍不清楚。该研究并未涉及 HBV 基因型或病毒学特征,限制了对 传播 动态或疾病严重程度的了解。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要开展有针对性的教育计划,以提高乙肝病毒的认识和知识,特别是男性、老年人(50-59 岁)和家庭主妇。它还强调了增加 HBV 检测和 Z​​XQTERMLQXZ 吸收的重要性,基于互联网的干预措施可能会利用对在线健康信息来源的高度依赖。

title: Gaps in the Cascade of Care Contribute to Poor Liver Cancer Outcomes Among People Living With Hepatitis B: A Multicenter Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in Australia, despite the availability of effective, subsidized antiviral therapy. We aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, HBV care cascade, and outcomes among people with HBV-related HCC in Victoria, Australia. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cohort study of all incident HCC cases across eight tertiary health networks in Victoria, Australia. Cases were identified retrospectively (January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019) and prospectively (January 1, 2020 to October 17, 2022). The primary outcome was the proportion of incident HCC attributable to HBV. Secondary outcomes included uptake of guideline-based antiviral therapy and surveillance and overall survival from HCC diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with treatment and surveillance uptake. RESULTS: Among 1203 incident HCC cases, 219 (18.2%) were HBV related. Most patients were male (89%) and of Asian ethnicity (60%). While 61% were aged 56-75 years, 25% were 36-55 years. Cirrhosis was present in 141 (64%), although 57 (26%) were newly diagnosed with cirrhosis at HCC presentation. The 121 (60%) patients were eligible for antiviral therapy. Linkage to specialist care was associated with treatment uptake (adjusted OR 8.4, 95% CI 4.3-16.1; p < 0.001). Surveillance enrolment at diagnosis was higher among HBV-related HCC compared with non-HBV HCC (48% vs. CONCLUSION: HBV remains a substantial contributor to HCC in Australia. Gaps in antiviral treatment and cirrhosis recognition persist, highlighting missed opportunities for prevention and early detection. Interventions to improve linkage to care and delivery of guideline-based HBV management are urgently needed.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in Australia despite the availability of effective antiviral therapy. The study addressed gaps in understanding why HBV-related HCC outcomes remain poor by examining the care cascade and clinical characteristics of affected individuals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicenter observational cohort study was conducted across eight tertiary health networks in Victoria, Australia. Incident HCC cases were identified retrospectively from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019 and prospectively from January 1, 2020 to October 17, 2022.
analysis.methods: The primary outcome was the proportion of incident HCC attributable to HBV, with secondary outcomes including uptake of guideline-based antiviral therapy and surveillance and overall survival. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with treatment and surveillance uptake.
analysis.main_results: Among 1203 incident HCC cases, 219 (18.2%) were HBV-related. Cirrhosis was present in 141 (64%) patients, with 57 (26%) newly diagnosed at HCC presentation. Linkage to specialist care was associated with higher treatment uptake (adjusted OR 8.4, 95% CI 4.3–16.1; p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that gaps in antiviral treatment and cirrhosis recognition persist, contributing to poor HCC outcomes. They highlight missed opportunities for prevention and early detection as key issues.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study underscores the need for interventions to improve linkage to care and delivery of guideline-based HBV management to reduce HBV-related HCC burden. analysis.summary_en: This multicenter observational cohort study in Victoria, Australia, examined the clinical characteristics and care cascade of 1203 incident hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases, of which 18.2% were HBV-related. Among HBV-related cases, 64% had cirrhosis, with 26% newly diagnosed at HCC presentation. Linkage to specialist care significantly increased antiviral therapy uptake (adjusted OR 8.4, 95% CI 4.3–16.1; p < 0.001). The authors identify persistent gaps in antiviral treatment and cirrhosis recognition as key contributors to poor HCC outcomes, emphasizing the urgent need for interventions to improve linkage to care and guideline-based HBV management.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调需要采取干预措施来改善护理和基于指南的乙肝治疗的联系,以减少乙肝相关的肝癌负担。它为高危人群中的 监测 和 治疗 策略提供了可行的见解。

title: A New Nomogram for Mortality Prediction Within 5 Years in Portal Vein Thrombosis due to Hepatitis B‐Related Cirrhosis
abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to develop a nomogram model intended for predicting long‐term mortality in patients suffering from hepatitis B‐related cirrhosis associated with Portal vein thrombosis (PVT). A total of 961 patients were recruited from January 2015 to December 2023, forming the training cohort. We analysed independent risk factors affecting 5‐year mortality through COX regression, from which we constructed a nomogram. To assess the nomogram's utility, we employed the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, C‐index, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The independent prognostic factors retained in the final model for patients with hepatitis B‐related cirrhosis complicated by PVT included age (HR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.06–1.11; p < 0.001), leukocyte count (WBC) (HR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.03–1.17; p = 0.002), and the neutrophil‐to‐lymphocyte ratio (NLR) (HR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.22–1.35; p < 0.001), along with serum sodium (HR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.90–0.98; p = 0.005). The AUROC values for the nomogram were 0.906 (95% CI: 0.891–0.921) in the training cohort and 0.910 (95% CI: 0.885–0.927) in the validation cohort, demonstrating improved performance and discriminatory ability compared to current models, including CTP and MELD scores. Age, leukocyte count (WBC), NLR, and serum sodium emerged as independent risk factors impacting prognosis for patients with hepatitis B cirrhosis and PVT within 5 years. The nomogram developed in this research holds significant potential for accurately predicting the outcomes of these patients within 5 years.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a nomogram model to predict 5-year mortality in patients with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis and Portal vein thrombosis (PVT). elements_zh.main_results: 训练 队列研究 中列线图的 AUROC 值为 0.906 (95% CI: 0.891–0.921),验证 队列研究 中的 AUROC 值为 0.910 (95% CI: 0.885–0.927),与 CTP 和 MELD 评分等当前模型相比,表现出更好的性能和辨别能力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为,与现有模型相比,列线图为预测乙型肝炎相关肝硬化和 PVT 患者的 5 年 死亡率 提供了更准确、更可靠的方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为乙型肝炎相关肝硬化和门静脉血栓患者开发更精确的 死亡率 预测工具提供信息,从而有可能改善临床决策和患者管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对单个 队列研究 的依赖以及可能存在未测量的混杂因素而受到限制。由于缺乏外部验证且使用单一数据集,证据强度中等。

title: Hepatitis B seroprevalence and knowledge awareness among spouses of reported Hepatitis B cases in Quzhou city: A cross-sectional study
abstract: This study investigated Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection prevalence and disease-related knowledge among spouses of reported HBV cases in Quzhou City to support family-based interventions reducing intra-familial transmission. In 2024, a cross-sectional survey was conducted in three randomly selected counties. Spouses (≥18y) of cases reported from Jan 2023 to Sep 2024 were interviewed with a structured questionnaire and tested for serological markers. Among 344 valid respondents, 161 provided blood samples. The HBsAg positivity rate was 11.80%. The rates for anti-HBs, anti-HBe, and anti-HBc were 60.87%, 23.60%, and 77.02%, respectively. No participant tested positive for HBeAg. Based on serological patterns, 12.42% were classified as susceptible, 9.94% had immunity from vaccination, and 50.93% had evidence of past infection. Overall HBV knowledge awareness rate was 36.69% with a pass rate of 22.09%. The awareness rates for the 10 specific knowledge items ranged from 6.40% to 62.21%. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that older age (≥60y: OR = 0.102, 95%CI:0.040 - 0.261), farmers/workers(OR = 0.335, 95%CI:0.155 - 0.723), and unawareness of personal infection status(OR = 0.364, 95%CI:0.159 - 0.833) were independently associated with lower knowledge. Most respondents preferred obtaining information through "hospitals/medical staff"(61.63%) and "online platforms/WeChat official accounts"(38.95%). Spouses have high HBsAg prevalence and poor HBV knowledge, indicating a substantial risk of intra-family transmission. Targeted health education, especially for the elderly, farmers/workers, and those unaware of their status, should be delivered through medical institutions to promote vaccination and regular testing, thereby reducing family‐clustered transmission.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 传播 仍然是中国的公共卫生重点,从指示病例到配偶的家庭内部 传播 有助于持续进行 传播。该研究旨在量化 HBV 血清流行率 并评估报告的 HBV 病例配偶之间的知识差距,为基于家庭的预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024年,在衢州市随机选择的三个县开展了一项横断面调查,纳入了2023年1月至2024年9月期间报告的乙型肝炎病例的18岁及以上配偶。

title: Hepatitis B Virus Infection: a Comprehensive Review of Viral Biology, Clinical Spectrum, and Preventive Strategies
abstract: Infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious health issue around the world, and one of the most common causes of long-term liver problems such as chronic liver disease and cirrhosis, and liver cancer. HBV is caused by the hepatitis B virus, which is part of the family of viruses called Hepadnaviridae and consists of a partially double-stranded DNA genome. Transmission occurs primarily through the exchange of blood and body fluids. The objective of this study was to collect available information about HBV infections and assess that information with respect to the following areas: epidemiology of HBV infection, viral biology, clinical features of HBV infection, diagnosis and treatment of HBV infection, and prevention of HBV infection. This study is a descriptive literature review based on the secondary research data acquired from the World Health Organization (WHO), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and peer-reviewed literature. A qualitative analysis process was used to extract the relevant information contained in the published literature. There are many different types of HBV infections. There are individuals who are asymptomatic carriers of HBV; individuals who have an acute HBV infection; individuals with chronic HBV infection; and individuals with cirrhosis and/or liver cancer caused by HBV. The diagnosis of HBV infection is determined by the presence of serological markers associated with the infection, such as HBsAg, HBeAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs, and HBV DNA levels. These markers also assist in determining whether or not the individual is infectious and how far progressed the disease is. Antiviral therapies available for treating HBV infection include tenofovir and entecavir which have been shown to effectively suppress viral replication but are unable to eliminate the covalently closed circular (ccc) DNA of the virus. Vaccination against HBV has demonstrated a reduction in the incident cases and remains the most effective means of prevention. The burden of HBV infection as a preventable global health issue continues. Properly diagnosing someone infected with HBV, treating the individual with an antiviral agent, and providing universal vaccination will be necessary to decrease the morbidity and mortality associated with HBV infection.

abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染是世界各地的一个严重的健康问题,也是慢性肝病、肝硬化和肝癌等长期肝脏问题的最常见原因之一。HBV 是由 乙型肝炎病毒 引起的,乙型肝炎病毒 是嗜肝DNA病毒科病毒家族的一部分,由部分双链 DNA 基因组 组成。传播 主要通过血液和体液的交换发生。本研究的目的是收集有关 HBV 感染的现有信息,并评估以下领域的信息:HBV 感染的 流行病学、病毒生物学、HBV 感染的临床特征、HBV 感染的 诊断 和 治疗 以及 HBV 感染的预防。本研究是基于从世界卫生组织 (WHO)、疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 获得的二手研究数据和同行评审文献的描述性文献综述。使用定性分析过程来提取已发表文献中包含的相关信息。乙型肝炎病毒感染有多种不同类型。有些人是无症状乙肝病毒携带者;患有急性乙型肝炎病毒感染的人;慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染者;以及患有由 HBV 引起的肝硬化和/或肝癌的个体。HBV 感染的 诊断 由与感染相关的血清学标志物的存在确定,例如 HBsAg、HBeAg、抗 HBc、抗 HBs 和 HBV DNA 水平。这些标记还有助于确定个体是否具有传染性以及疾病的进展程度。可用于治疗 HBV 感染的 抗病毒药物 疗法包括替诺福韦和恩替卡韦,它们已被证明可以有效抑制病毒复制,但无法消除病毒的共价闭合环状 (ccc) DNA。疫苗接种 针对 HBV 已证明事件病例减少,并且仍然是最有效的预防手段。作为可预防的全球健康问题,乙型肝炎病毒感染的负担仍在继续。正确诊断 HBV 感染者、用 抗病毒药物 药物治疗个体以及提供通用 疫苗接种 对于降低与 HBV 感染相关的发病率和 死亡率 是必要的。

title: Differential Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Glycan Isomer Kinetics Between Tenofovir Alafenamide and Entecavir: Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Stratification in Hepatitis B e Antigen-Positive Patients.
abstract: Nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy suppresses hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA, but residual hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk persists. O-glycosylated hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) uniquely reflects virion burden. We evaluated the impact of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) versus entecavir (ETV) on 48-week HBsAgGi kinetics and its utility in stratifying HCC risk in 90 NA-naïve patients (ETV: 73; TAF: 17). A favourable response was defined as a reduction or maintenance of low HBsAgGi levels. TAF independently predicted a favourable response compared with ETV (penalised odds ratio 3.60, p = 0.030). A significant interaction occurred between HBeAg status and HBsAgGi response in relation to HCC development (p = 0.038). In HBeAg-positive patients, a poor response was associated with increased HCC risk (hazard ratio 7.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.96-20.35, p = 0.001); however, the exact magnitude warrants cautious interpretation due to wide CIs. This association was absent in HBeAg-negative cases. Adding HBsAgGi response to the aMAP score improved long-term HCC prediction exclusively in the HBeAg-positive cohort. As the assay targets genotype C-specific O-glycosylation, the findings cannot be generalised to genotypes A, B, or D. In conclusion, on-treatment HBsAgGi response is a specific surrogate marker for stratifying residual HCC risk in HBeAg-positive patients, and TAF is more effective than ETV in inducing these favourable kinetics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Despite nucleos(t)ide analog therapy suppressing HBV DNA, residual hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk persists, creating a need for better risk-stratification markers. The study asked whether on-treatment hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) kinetics could distinguish HCC risk and whether tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) outperforms entecavir (ETV) in modulating these kinetics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a prospective cohort study of 90 NA-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients initiating either TAF (n=17) or ETV (n=73) and followed for 48 weeks. The population comprised HBeAg-positive and HBeAg-negative adults receiving standard-of-care antiviral therapy.
analysis.methods: HBsAgGi was quantified using a genotype C-specific O-glycosylation assay; a favourable response was defined as reduction or maintenance of low HBsAgGi levels. Logistic regression with penalised estimation evaluated predictors of favourable HBsAgGi kinetics, and Cox models assessed HCC risk associations.
analysis.main_results: TAF independently predicted a favourable HBsAgGi response versus ETV (penalised odds ratio 3.60, p=0.030). In HBeAg-positive patients, poor HBsAgGi response was associated with increased HCC risk (hazard ratio 7.34, 95% CI 1.96–20.35, p=0.001), whereas no association was observed in HBeAg-negative patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret on-treatment HBsAgGi response as a specific surrogate marker for residual HCC risk in HBeAg-positive patients and conclude that TAF induces more favourable HBsAgGi kinetics than ETV. This is the first report linking HBsAgGi kinetics to HCC risk stratification during NA therapy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that incorporating HBsAgGi response into existing HCC risk scores (e.g., aMAP) could refine long-term risk prediction in HBeAg-positive patients. They also imply a potential advantage of TAF over ETV in reducing HCC risk via improved HBsAgGi kinetics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The genotype C-specific assay limits generalisability to other HBV genotypes. The wide confidence intervals around the HCC hazard ratio warrant cautious interpretation, and the study’s modest sample size and single-centre design constrain external validity. Overall evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective cohort study of 90 NA-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients found that tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) more effectively induces favourable hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) kinetics over 48 weeks than entecavir (ETV). title: Hepatitis B and D burden in Uzbekistan: comprehensive analysis of seroprevalence and risk correlates from a countrywide study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Uzbekistan faces a substantial burden of hepatitis B and D virus (HBV and HDV) infections despite implementing universal hepatitis B vaccination in 1998. Regional variation in disease distribution and contemporary transmission dynamics remain inadequately characterized. Our objective was to evaluate the geographically stratified prevalence of HBV and HDV, while also identifying the key risk factors fueling transmission within the adult population of Uzbekistan. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional study of 10,552 adults across seven regions of Uzbekistan from July 2022 to June 2024. Participants were selected using stratified random sampling from a parent cohort of 1,048,575 individuals. Serological testing included hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), antibodies to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc), anti-HDV antibodies, and viral RNA detection. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent risk factors for HBV and HDV infections. RESULTS: Overall HBsAg prevalence was 4.7% (95% CI: 4.3-5.1%), with substantial geographic heterogeneity ranging from 3.2% in Tashkent to 6.3% in Bukhara. Among HBsAg-positive individuals, 68.1% had detectable HBV DNA and 12.7% had HDV superinfection. HDV RNA prevalence among HBV DNA-positive individuals ranged from 2.5% to 23.7% across regions. Age-cohort analysis demonstrated vaccination program impact, with older unvaccinated adults bearing disproportionate disease burden. Female sex associated with 31% lower odds of chronic HBsAg carriage. Married status, healthcare-associated exposures, and body piercings correlated with increased anti-HBc positivity. Remarkably, sharing personal hygiene items showed striking HDV-specific association (aOR 2.34, 95% CI: 1.16-4.74; P = 0.02) but no association with HBV markers, suggesting distinct transmission pathways for HDV superinfection. CONCLUSIONS: Persistent HBV burden with notable regional clustering and HDV superinfection necessitates targeted interventions. The identification of personal hygiene item sharing as a specific HDV transmission route provides an actionable household-level prevention target. Intensified screening and treatment of unvaccinated adults remain critical for hepatitis elimination efforts.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted in Uzbekistan from July 2022 to June 2024, enrolling 10,552 adults selected via stratified random sampling from a parent cohort of 1,048,575 individuals across seven regions.
analysis.methods: Serological testing included hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), antibodies to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc), and viral RNA detection, with multivariate logistic regression used to identify independent risk factors for HBV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This nationwide cross-sectional study in Uzbekistan assessed the burden of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection among 10,552 adults from July 2022 to June 2024, using stratified random sampling from a parent cohort of over one million individuals. Among HBsAg-positive participants, 68.1% had detectable HBV DNA, and 12.7% had hepatitis D virus (HDV) superinfection. title_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦的乙型和丁型肝炎负担:对 血清流行率 的综合分析以及全国范围研究的风险相关性
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Uzbekistan faces a substantial burden of hepatitis B and D virus (HBV and HDV) infections despite implementing universal hepatitis B vaccination in 1998. Regional variation in disease distribution and contemporary transmission dynamics remain inadequately characterized. Our objective was to evaluate the geographically stratified prevalence of HBV and HDV, while also identifying the key risk factors fueling transmission within the adult population of Uzbekistan. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional study of 10,552 adults across seven regions of Uzbekistan from July 2022 to June 2024. Participants were selected using stratified random sampling from a parent cohort of 1,048,575 individuals. Serological testing included hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), antibodies to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc), anti-HDV antibodies, and viral RNA detection. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent risk factors for HBV and HDV infections. RESULTS: Overall HBsAg prevalence was 4.7% (95% CI: 4.3-5.1%), with substantial geographic heterogeneity ranging from 3.2% in Tashkent to 6.3% in Bukhara. Among HBsAg-positive individuals, 68.1% had detectable HBV DNA and 12.7% had HDV superinfection. HDV RNA prevalence among HBV DNA-positive individuals ranged from 2.5% to 23.7% across regions. Age-cohort analysis demonstrated vaccination program impact, with older unvaccinated adults bearing disproportionate disease burden. Female sex associated with 31% lower odds of chronic HBsAg carriage. Married status, healthcare-associated exposures, and body piercings correlated with increased anti-HBc positivity. Remarkably, sharing personal hygiene items showed striking HDV-specific association (aOR 2.34, 95% CI: 1.16-4.74; P = 0.02) but no association with HBV markers, suggesting distinct transmission pathways for HDV superinfection. CONCLUSIONS: Persistent HBV burden with notable regional clustering and HDV superinfection necessitates targeted interventions. The identification of personal hygiene item sharing as a specific HDV transmission route provides an actionable household-level prevention target. Intensified screening and treatment of unvaccinated adults remain critical for hepatitis elimination efforts.
