title: Development and validation of GADA model for diagnosing hepatocellular carcinoma in Chinese hepatitis B patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection accounts for more than 40% of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases worldwide. The GALAD (Gender, Age, alpha fetoprotein heterogeneity [AFP-L3], AFP, and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin [PIVKA-II/DCP]) model has potential for enhancing HCC diagnosis. However, its diagnostic performance in HBV-associated chronic liver disease requires further optimization. This study aimed to establish a diagnostic model for HBV-associated HCC. METHODS: The data from 2190 patients with HBV-related liver diseases, including chronic hepatitis B (CHB), cirrhosis, and HCC were analysed. The GADA model was developed by omitting AFP-L3 for improved accessibility, and its performance was assessed via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Validation was performed on 20,908 patients across ten hospitals. RESULTS: The simplified GADA model demonstrated exceptional diagnostic performance in identifying HBV-related HCC in the modeling group, achieving an AUC of 0.940 (95% CI, 0.927-0.952), with a sensitivity and specificity of 82.57% and 91.53%, respectively, surpassing the original GALAD model's AUC of 0.907 (95% CI, 0.891-0.921). In the internal validation cohort, the GADA model had an AUC of 0.935 (95% CI, 0.914-0.953), sensitivity of 82.04%, and specificity of 92.65%. For early-stage HCC detection, the AUC in the modeling group was 0.858 (95% CI, 0.837-0.877), and in the internal validation group was 0.868 (95% CI, 0.836-0.895), significantly better than the original GALAD model. External validation with 20,908 participants yielded an AUC of 0.919 (95% CI, 0.916-0.923), with sensitivity of 86.00% and specificity 81.88%. For early-stage HCC diagnosis, the AUC was 0.903 (95% CI: 0.898-0.907), with sensitivity of 88.16% and specificity 74.50%. CONCLUSIONS: The GADA model shows exceptional promise for diagnosing HBV-related HCC, enhancing early detection and reducing misdiagnosis rates. Its clinical utility is supported by robust validation, indicating significant implications for patient prognosis and treatment options.

The GALAD (Gender, Age, alpha fetoprotein heterogeneity [AFP-L3], AFP, and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin [PIVKA-II/DCP]) model has potential for enhancing HCC diagnosis. However, its diagnostic performance in HBV-associated chronic liver disease requires further optimization. This study aimed to establish a diagnostic model for HBV-associated HCC. METHODS: The data from 2190 patients with HBV-related liver diseases, including chronic hepatitis B (CHB), cirrhosis, and HCC were analysed. The GADA model was developed by omitting AFP-L3 for improved accessibility, and its performance was assessed via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Validation was performed on 20,908 patients across ten hospitals. RESULTS: The simplified GADA model demonstrated exceptional diagnostic performance in identifying HBV-related HCC in the modeling group, achieving an AUC of 0.940 (95% CI, 0.927-0.952), with a sensitivity and specificity of 82.57% and 91.53%, respectively, surpassing the original GALAD model's AUC of 0.907 (95% CI, 0.891-0.921). In the internal validation cohort, the GADA model had an AUC of 0.935 (95% CI, 0.914-0.953), sensitivity of 82.04%, and specificity of 92.65%. For early-stage HCC detection, the AUC in the modeling group was 0.858 (95% CI, 0.837-0.877), and in the internal validation group was 0.868 (95% CI, 0.836-0.895), significantly better than the original GALAD model. External validation with 20,908 participants yielded an AUC of 0.919 (95% CI, 0.916-0.923), with sensitivity of 86.00% and specificity 81.88%. For early-stage HCC diagnosis, the AUC was 0.903 (95% CI: 0.898-0.907), with sensitivity of 88.16% and specificity 74.50%. CONCLUSIONS: The GADA model shows exceptional promise for diagnosing HBV-related HCC, enhancing early detection and reducing misdiagnosis rates. Its clinical utility is supported by robust validation, indicating significant implications for patient prognosis and treatment options.

title: Geospatial Discrepancy of Chronic Hepatitis B and Hepatitis D Testing in Alberta: A Population-Based Spatial Analysis.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The geographic distribution of CHB and alignment of anti-HDV testing with CHB burden remain poorly defined. We aimed to examine if anti-HDV testing and seropositivity align with areas of highest CHB burden. Adults with CHB (2014-2022) were identified using a validated serologic algorithm in the provincial laboratory database capturing HBV/HDV serology. Cases were geolocated to Aggregate Dissemination Areas (ADAs), linked to Alberta Health Services zones and rural-urban continuum levels. Age- and sex-standardized CHB prevalence was calculated per ADA using the 2016 Canadian Census. Descriptive mapping, global spatial autocorrelation and local hotspot analysis were used to assess spatial clustering. Among 8317 persons with CHB, the provincial age- and sex-standardized prevalence was 1.70 per 1000 population (95% CI, 1.66-1.74). Prevalence ranged from 2.15 per 1000 in metropolitan areas to 0.40 per 1000 in remote regions and was higher in Calgary than Edmonton (2.53 vs. Overall, 17.5% of CHB patients were tested for anti-HDV, and 4.1% of those tested were anti-HDV positive. CHB prevalence hotspots were concentrated in metropolitan ADAs, whereas hotspots of anti-HDV testing and positivity showed only partial overlap with these high-burden areas. CHB burden in Alberta is geographically clustered, particularly within specific neighbourhoods of metropolitan cities, whereas anti-HDV testing remains infrequent and only partially aligned with high-burden areas. Reflex or systematic anti-HDV testing, paired with geographically informed outreach, may improve case detection.

title_zh: 艾伯塔省 慢性乙型肝炎 和丁型肝炎检测的地理空间差异:基于人群的空间分析。
source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The geographic distribution of CHB and alignment of anti-HDV testing with CHB burden remain poorly defined. We aimed to examine if anti-HDV testing and seropositivity align with areas of highest CHB burden. Adults with CHB (2014-2022) were identified using a validated serologic algorithm in the provincial laboratory database capturing HBV/HDV serology. Cases were geolocated to Aggregate Dissemination Areas (ADAs), linked to Alberta Health Services zones and rural-urban continuum levels. Age- and sex-standardized CHB prevalence was calculated per ADA using the 2016 Canadian Census. Descriptive mapping, global spatial autocorrelation and local hotspot analysis were used to assess spatial clustering. Among 8317 persons with CHB, the provincial age- and sex-standardized prevalence was 1.70 per 1000 population (95% CI, 1.66-1.74). Prevalence ranged from 2.15 per 1000 in metropolitan areas to 0.40 per 1000 in remote regions and was higher in Calgary than Edmonton (2.53 vs. Overall, 17.5% of CHB patients were tested for anti-HDV, and 4.1% of those tested were anti-HDV positive. CHB prevalence hotspots were concentrated in metropolitan ADAs, whereas hotspots of anti-HDV testing and positivity showed only partial overlap with these high-burden areas. CHB burden in Alberta is geographically clustered, particularly within specific neighbourhoods of metropolitan cities, whereas anti-HDV testing remains infrequent and only partially aligned with high-burden areas. Reflex or systematic anti-HDV testing, paired with geographically informed outreach, may improve case detection.

title: Deep Sequencing of Hepatitis B Virus Reveals Clinically Relevant Low-Frequency Variants Among People Living with HIV in Botswana
abstract: (1) Background: The Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is characterized by extensive genetic diversity, including low-frequency variants that contribute to disease progression. We aimed to characterize low-frequency variants and evaluate their potential clinical impact. (2) Methods: We utilized 104 HBV near-full-length sequences generated using next-generation sequencing (NGS) from people living with HIV (PLHIV). We used an in-house bioinformatics suite (HBVgenomeR v5.9.7) to filter for low-frequency variants (5–50%), which were compared to escape and drug resistance mutations (DRMs) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)-associated mutations reported at the consensus level. Unclassified variants were characterized by HBV open reading frames (ORFs) to determine mutation frequency per genomic region. (3) Results: A total of six escape mutations were detected in 8/104 (7.7%) sequences, with surfaceN131T being the most prevalent (5/8). We also observed six DRMs in 30/104 (28.8%), with rtV173L being the most prevalent (21/30). Truncation mutations were also observed with rtA181T/sW172* and rtM204I/sW196L being the most prevalent. A total of 8/104 (7.7%) sequences had four variants associated with HCC. The xP46S was the highest observed HCC-associated mutation at 5/8. We report 1152 unique uncharacterized variants across all ORFs, and these were found in 94/104 (90.4%) sequences. The RNaseH domain had the highest burden (330/1152, 28.6%). (4) Conclusions: Deep sequencing results identified clinically significant mutations, including those below the 20% detection limit of traditional sequencing, that would go unreported. This highlights the possible underreporting of mutational burden in people living with HBV/HIV, indicating the importance of deep sequencing to aid in HBV/HIV understanding and management.

title: Antiviral profile of hepatitis B virus capsid assembly modulator ALG-001075, the parent of pevifoscorvir sodium.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains an important unmet medical need with 240 million patients worldwide. The HBV capsid assembly process has emerged as a key target for more efficient antiviral intervention. Pevifoscorvir sodium (ALG-000184), an oral prodrug of the potent HBV capsid assembly modulator (CAM) ALG-001075 showed significant reductions in HBV DNA, HBV RNA and other viral antigens (HBsAg, HBcrAg and HBeAg) in Phase I clinical participants with chronic HBV infection. We aim to characterize the antiviral properties of ALG-001075. ALG-001075 is a highly potent CAM that inhibited HBV DNA production in cellular settings with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 value of only 22 nM. ALG-001075 was shown to induce the formation of empty, but not aberrant viral particles as demonstrated by fluorescence quenching, electron microscopy, size-exclusion chromatography, immunofluorescent staining and NMR analysis, thereby classifying it as a CAM-E. Notably, solid-state NMR spectra of wild-type capsids in the presence of ALG-001075 revealed a characteristic CAM-E fingerprint at atomic resolution. ALG-001075 showed potent antiviral activity against HBV strains from genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant virus strains and known CAM-resistance mutations, with the exception of T33N, T33P and V124G, which induced 6-to-28-fold loss in ALG-001075 activity. The in vivo efficacy of ALG-001075 was confirmed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice, where ALG-001075 demonstrated up to 5 log10 reduction in circulating HBV DNA levels. Because of its robust antiviral potency and favorable preclinical resistance profile, ALG-001075 was selected for further clinical development under the form of its prodrug pevifoscorvir sodium.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection represents a major global health burden with 240 million patients worldwide and limited therapeutic options. The study addresses the unmet need for more effective antiviral interventions by targeting the HBV capsid assembly process, which is critical for viral replication.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterizes the antiviral properties of the HBV capsid assembly modulator ALG-001075, the parent compound of pevifoscorvir sodium. It synthesizes preclinical data including cellular models, structural analyses, and in vivo efficacy studies in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice.
analysis.methods: ALG-001075 was evaluated for antiviral potency using cellular assays to determine EC50 and EC99.9 values. Structural characterization involved fluorescence quenching, electron microscopy, size-exclusion chromatography, immunofluorescent staining, NMR analysis, and solid-state NMR spectroscopy. In vivo efficacy was assessed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice.
analysis.main_results: ALG-001075 demonstrated potent antiviral activity with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 value of 22 nM. It induced the formation of empty viral particles without aberrant structures and produced a characteristic CAM-E fingerprint in solid-state NMR spectra. The compound showed activity against HBV genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant strains, and most CAM-resistance mutations, except T33N, T33P, and V124G. In vivo, ALG-001075 achieved up to a 5 log10 reduction in circulating HBV DNA levels in mice.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish ALG-001075 as a highly potent and mechanistically distinct HBV capsid assembly modulator (CAM-E) with a favorable resistance profile. The atomic-resolution structural fingerprint and broad genotypic coverage represent novel contributions to HBV antiviral development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results support the clinical advancement of ALG-001075 as a promising therapeutic candidate for chronic HBV infection, particularly against resistant strains and diverse genotypes. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to preclinical and early clinical data summarized in the abstract, with no reported details on study design, sample sizes, or statistical analyses. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the absence of comprehensive methodological and outcome reporting.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes ALG-001075, a potent hepatitis B virus (HBV) capsid assembly modulator (CAM) and the parent compound of pevifoscorvir sodium, addressing the unmet need for improved HBV therapies. The compound exhibits exceptional antiviral potency with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 of 22 nM, inducing the formation of empty viral particles without aberrant structures. Structural analyses via NMR and microscopy reveal a distinct CAM-E fingerprint at atomic resolution. ALG-001075 demonstrates broad activity across HBV genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant strains, and most CAM-resistance mutations, with reduced efficacy against T33N, T33P, and V124G. In vivo efficacy is confirmed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice, where the compound achieves up to a 5 log10 reduction in HBV DNA. elements_zh.main_results: ALG-001075 表现出有效的 抗病毒药物 活性,EC50 值低于 1 nM,EC99.9 值为 22 nM。它诱导形成没有异常结构的空病毒颗粒,并在固态 NMR 光谱中产生特征性 CAM-E 指纹。该化合物对 HBV 基因型 A-J、核苷类似物耐药菌株和大多数 CAM 耐药菌株 突变(T33N、T33P 和 V124G 除外)表现出活性。在体内,ALG-001075 使小鼠循环 HBV DNA 水平降低了 5 log10。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection represents a major global health burden with 240 million patients worldwide and limited therapeutic options. The study addresses the unmet need for more effective antiviral interventions by targeting the HBV capsid assembly process, which is critical for viral replication.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study characterizes the antiviral properties of the HBV capsid assembly modulator ALG-001075, the parent compound of pevifoscorvir sodium. It synthesizes preclinical data including cellular models, structural analyses, and in vivo efficacy studies in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice.
analysis_en.methods: ALG-001075 was evaluated for antiviral potency using cellular assays to determine EC50 and EC99.9 values. Structural characterization involved fluorescence quenching, electron microscopy, size-exclusion chromatography, immunofluorescent staining, NMR analysis, and solid-state NMR spectroscopy. In vivo efficacy was assessed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice.
analysis_en.main_results: ALG-001075 demonstrated potent antiviral activity with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 value of 22 nM. It induced the formation of empty viral particles without aberrant structures and produced a characteristic CAM-E fingerprint in solid-state NMR spectra. The compound showed activity against HBV genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant strains, and most CAM-resistance mutations, except T33N, T33P, and V124G. In vivo, ALG-001075 achieved up to a 5 log10 reduction in circulating HBV DNA levels in mice.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish ALG-001075 as a highly potent and mechanistically distinct HBV capsid assembly modulator (CAM-E) with a favorable resistance profile. The atomic-resolution structural fingerprint and broad genotypic coverage represent novel contributions to HBV antiviral development.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results support the clinical advancement of ALG-001075 as a promising therapeutic candidate for chronic HBV infection, particularly against resistant strains and diverse genotypes. Its potent antiviral activity and mechanistic specificity may inform future treatment strategies and resistance surveillance.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to preclinical and early clinical data summarized in the abstract, with no reported details on study design, sample sizes, or statistical analyses. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the absence of comprehensive methodological and outcome reporting.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 衣壳组装调节剂 ALG-001075(pevifoscorvir 钠的母体)的 抗病毒药物 概况。
source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains an important unmet medical need with 240 million patients worldwide. The HBV capsid assembly process has emerged as a key target for more efficient antiviral intervention. Pevifoscorvir sodium (ALG-000184), an oral prodrug of the potent HBV capsid assembly modulator (CAM) ALG-001075 showed significant reductions in HBV DNA, HBV RNA and other viral antigens (HBsAg, HBcrAg and HBeAg) in Phase I clinical participants with chronic HBV infection. We aim to characterize the antiviral properties of ALG-001075. ALG-001075 is a highly potent CAM that inhibited HBV DNA production in cellular settings with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 value of only 22 nM. ALG-001075 was shown to induce the formation of empty, but not aberrant viral particles as demonstrated by fluorescence quenching, electron microscopy, size-exclusion chromatography, immunofluorescent staining and NMR analysis, thereby classifying it as a CAM-E. Notably, solid-state NMR spectra of wild-type capsids in the presence of ALG-001075 revealed a characteristic CAM-E fingerprint at atomic resolution. ALG-001075 showed potent antiviral activity against HBV strains from genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant virus strains and known CAM-resistance mutations, with the exception of T33N, T33P and V124G, which induced 6-to-28-fold loss in ALG-001075 activity. The in vivo efficacy of ALG-001075 was confirmed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice, where ALG-001075 demonstrated up to 5 log10 reduction in circulating HBV DNA levels. Because of its robust antiviral potency and favorable preclinical resistance profile, ALG-001075 was selected for further clinical development under the form of its prodrug pevifoscorvir sodium.

title: Validation of a Point-Of-Care Ultrasound for Hepatitis Among Front-Line Healthcare Workers Managing Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Zambia.
abstract: To close gaps in implementing care of people with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in resource-limited settings, we evaluated the accuracy of a novel liver point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) protocol for hepatitis (PUSH) among front-line non-radiology healthcare workers in Zambia. At University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, Zambia, from March to June 2024, we trained four nurses and six physicians with experience in HBV management, but not in ultrasound (US), in the PUSH protocol, which includes visualizing the liver in three windows (epigastric, subcostal and right transcostal) to identify cirrhosis-suggestive features and liver lesions suspicious for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Then, consecutive adult participants with chronic hepatitis B (PWHB) alone or HBV/HIV coinfection underwent PUSH with operators blinded to clinical data. We evaluated the accuracy of PUSH for significant fibrosis and cirrhosis using transient elastography (TE) as the reference standard test (RST) and for liver lesions that were possible HCC using a comprehensive abdominal ultrasound by an experienced radiographer as the RST. Nonparametric analysis of the receiver operating curve (ROC) for PUSH was adjusted for operator type (doctor vs. nurse), sex and HIV status. Among 197 PWHBs analysed, 69.5% were taking HBV antivirals and 27.9% had HBV/HIV. According to RSTs, 17.7% of PWHBs had significant fibrosis, 11.6% had cirrhosis and 3.5% had liver lesions. PUSH had low accuracy for significant fibrosis, with sensitivity of 8.3% (17.5-41.4), specificity of 100.0% (96.1-100) and an area under the curve (AUROC) of 0.54 (0.43-0.65), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis, with sensitivity of 60.9% (38.5-80.3), specificity of 97.7% (94.2-99.4) and AUROC of 0.79 (0.69-0.89), and higher accuracy for liver lesions, with 85.7% (42.1-99.6) sensitivity, 98.4% (95.5-99.7) specificity, AUROC of 0.92 (0.78-1.00). After an expedited training, front-line nurses and physicians treating HBV in Zambia were able to use PUSH to diagnose cirrhosis with moderate accuracy and liver lesions with high accuracy, although confidence intervals around performance estimates were wide. Liver POCUS including PUSH may be useful in HBV management when laboratory systems and TE are lacking.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains under-managed in resource-limited settings due to diagnostic access barriers, prompting the need for accurate, point-of-care tools for front-line healthcare workers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: At University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, Zambia, from March to June 2024, four nurses and six physicians with HBV management experience but no ultrasound training were trained in the PUSH protocol and performed point-of-care ultrasound on consecutive adults with chronic HBV alone or HBV/HIV coinfection.
analysis.methods: PUSH assessed liver cirrhosis-suggestive features and lesions suspicious for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) using three windows (epigastric, subcostal, right transcostal), with operators blinded to clinical data; accuracy was evaluated against transient elastography for fibrosis/cirrhosis and comprehensive abdominal ultrasound for HCC, with nonparametric ROC analysis adjusted for operator type, sex and HIV status.
analysis.main_results: Among 197 participants, 17.7% had significant fibrosis, 11.6% had cirrhosis and 3.5% had liver lesions; PUSH showed low accuracy for significant fibrosis (sensitivity 8.3%, specificity 100.0%, AUROC 0.54), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis (sensitivity 60.9%, specificity 97.7%, AUROC 0.79) and high accuracy for liver lesions (sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 98.4%, AUROC 0.92).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that after expedited training, front-line nurses and physicians could use PUSH to diagnose cirrhosis with moderate accuracy and liver lesions with high accuracy, noting wide confidence intervals around performance estimates.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Liver POCUS including PUSH may be useful for HBV management in settings lacking laboratory systems and transient elastography, potentially improving early detection of cirrhosis and HCC.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s small sample size and wide confidence intervals limit precision, and the training cohort was small, which may affect generalisability; evidence strength is assessed as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated a novel point-of-care ultrasound protocol (PUSH) for diagnosing liver disease among front-line healthcare workers in Zambia managing chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. After brief training, nurses and physicians used PUSH to assess liver fibrosis, cirrhosis and lesions, comparing results with transient elastography and expert ultrasound. PUSH showed low accuracy for significant fibrosis but moderate accuracy for cirrhosis and high accuracy for liver lesions suspicious for hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors suggest PUSH could support HBV care where laboratory and imaging resources are limited, though wide confidence intervals and a small training cohort constrain precision.

title_zh: 在赞比亚处理 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染的一线医护人员中验证肝炎护理点超声检查。
source_body_en: To close gaps in implementing care of people with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in resource-limited settings, we evaluated the accuracy of a novel liver point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) protocol for hepatitis (PUSH) among front-line non-radiology healthcare workers in Zambia. At University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, Zambia, from March to June 2024, we trained four nurses and six physicians with experience in HBV management, but not in ultrasound (US), in the PUSH protocol, which includes visualizing the liver in three windows (epigastric, subcostal and right transcostal) to identify cirrhosis-suggestive features and liver lesions suspicious for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Then, consecutive adult participants with chronic hepatitis B (PWHB) alone or HBV/HIV coinfection underwent PUSH with operators blinded to clinical data. We evaluated the accuracy of PUSH for significant fibrosis and cirrhosis using transient elastography (TE) as the reference standard test (RST) and for liver lesions that were possible HCC using a comprehensive abdominal ultrasound by an experienced radiographer as the RST. Nonparametric analysis of the receiver operating curve (ROC) for PUSH was adjusted for operator type (doctor vs. nurse), sex and HIV status. Among 197 PWHBs analysed, 69.5% were taking HBV antivirals and 27.9% had HBV/HIV. According to RSTs, 17.7% of PWHBs had significant fibrosis, 11.6% had cirrhosis and 3.5% had liver lesions. PUSH had low accuracy for significant fibrosis, with sensitivity of 8.3% (17.5-41.4), specificity of 100.0% (96.1-100) and an area under the curve (AUROC) of 0.54 (0.43-0.65), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis, with sensitivity of 60.9% (38.5-80.3), specificity of 97.7% (94.2-99.4) and AUROC of 0.79 (0.69-0.89), and higher accuracy for liver lesions, with 85.7% (42.1-99.6) sensitivity, 98.4% (95.5-99.7) specificity, AUROC of 0.92 (0.78-1.00). After an expedited training, front-line nurses and physicians treating HBV in Zambia were able to use PUSH to diagnose cirrhosis with moderate accuracy and liver lesions with high accuracy, although confidence intervals around performance estimates were wide. Liver POCUS including PUSH may be useful in HBV management when laboratory systems and TE are lacking.

title: Molecular Characterization and Genotypic Distribution of Hepatitis B Virus Isolates in Iraq: Prevalence of Drug Resistance Mutations
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most pervasive viral threats worldwide, posing a significant risk to millions. Due to the absence of proofreading activity during reverse transcription, HBV exhibits a high genetic variability. To date, ten distinct HBV genotypes have been identified globally, associated with varying disease outcomes, including progression to cirrhosis and carcinoma, as well as responses to antivirals. Consequently, genotypic analysis and molecular characterization of HBV are critical for optimizing therapeutic strategies. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of HBV genotypes among Iraqi patients and to characterize their molecular profiles. Therefore, a modified protocol was used to improve sequencing success rates in samples with low amplification yields. Results: HBV/D was predominant in the study cohort (100%). Subgenotypic analysis revealed that HBV/D1 accounts for the majority of cases (68%), followed by D3 (32%). Sequences of 16 isolates were deposited in NCBI under accession numbers PV068280; PV124387–PV124397; and PV172617–PV172620. Moreover, the analysis of antiviral resistance indicated that 47% (32/68) of HBV/D1 isolates exhibited drug resistance, with all resistant isolates showing mutations associated with Lamivudine resistance (100%), Entecavir intermediate/high resistance (81% and 19%, respectively), and Telbivudine (25%). These findings underscore the dominance of genotype D, particularly HBV/D1 among Iraqi patients. To our knowledge, this is the first local study to correlate genotypic variation with drug resistance and highlight the importance of continuous surveillance for antiviral resistance to guide effective treatment strategies.

title: The Uncared-for Carers: A Cross-Sectional Study of Hepatitis B Vaccination Uptake and Predictors Among Volunteer Healthcare Workers in Zambia: HBV Vaccination Uptake Among Volunteer HCWs.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) poses a major occupational risk to healthcare workers (HCWs), particularly in moderate-to-high‐prevalence settings such as Zambia. Despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine, coverage among HCWs remains suboptimal. Among HCWs, volunteer HCWs face unique challenges, including financial barriers, that increase their risk. However, they are often overlooked in research. The present study aimed to determine HBV vaccination uptake and its predictors among volunteer HCWs in Zambia. METHODS: This national cross-sectional study utilized a self-administered semi-structured online questionnaire to collect data from volunteer HCWs from October 3 to November 26 2024. Using R version 4.6.0 and Stata version 17, descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed. A two-sided p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: Among the 173 participants, 51 (29.5%) reported being vaccinated. Of the 51, 23 (45.1%) had received one dose, 4 (7.8%) two doses, and 24 (47.1%) at least three doses (fully vaccinated). In the multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression model, participants who had access to HBV vaccination programs during training were significantly more likely to be vaccinated than those without such programs (p < 0.001). Availability of HBV testing services at the health facility was also independently associated with vaccination uptake (p = 0.006). Increasing age was associated with slightly higher odds of vaccination (p = 0.025). Gender and place of education were not independently associated with vaccination uptake after adjustment. CONCLUSION: HBV vaccination coverage among volunteer HCWs in Zambia was low. Vaccination programs during training, age and the availability of HBV testing services were important factors associated with vaccine uptake. Strengthening institutional HBV prevention programs may improve vaccination coverage and reduce occupational risk among HCWs.

abstract_zh: 背景和目标:乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 对医护人员 (HCW) 构成重大职业风险,特别是在赞比亚等中度至高 患病率 环境中。尽管有安全有效的 疫苗,但医护人员的覆盖率仍然不理想。在医护人员中,志愿医护人员面临着独特的挑战,包括财务障碍,这增加了他们的风险。然而,它们在研究中经常被忽视。本研究旨在确定赞比亚志愿医护人员中 HBV 疫苗接种 的摄取情况及其预测因素。方法:这项全国横断面研究采用自我管理的半结构化在线问卷来收集 2024 年 10 月 3 日至 11 月 26 日期间志愿医护人员的数据。使用 R 版本 4.6.0 和 Stata 版本 17 进行描述性和推论统计分析。两侧 p 值 < 0.05 被认为具有统计显着性。结果:在 173 名参与者中,51 人 (29.5%) 报告已接种疫苗。在 51 人中,23 人 (45.1%) 接种了一剂疫苗,4 人 (7.8%) 接种了两剂疫苗,24 人 (47.1%) 至少接种了三剂疫苗(完全接种)。在多变量 Firth 惩罚逻辑回归模型中,在培训期间参与 HBV 疫苗接种 计划的参与者比没有此类计划的参与者更有可能接种疫苗 (p < 0.001)。卫生机构提供的 HBV 检测服务也与 疫苗接种 的吸收率独立相关 (p = 0.006)。年龄的增加与 疫苗接种 的几率稍高相关(p = 0.025)。调整后,性别和教育地点与 疫苗接种 的吸收率没有独立相关。结论:赞比亚志愿医护人员中 HBV 疫苗接种 覆盖率较低。培训期间的 疫苗接种 计划、年龄和 HBV 检测服务的可用性是与 ZX​​QTERMAAQXZ 吸收相关的重要因素。加强机构乙型肝炎预防计划可以提高 疫苗接种 的覆盖率并降低医护人员的职业风险。

title: The magnitude of early hepatitis B RNA and DNA declines directly inform capsid assembly modulator effectiveness
abstract: Capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) are a promising class of antiviral treatments for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Several CAMs have been evaluated in clinical trials but there is no simple method to estimate their in vivo antiviral effectiveness. We performed viral dynamics modeling of the intracellular and extracellular dynamics of HBV RNA, HBV DNA, and ALT during phase I trials of two CAMs, vebicorvir and ABI-H2158, which inhibit the encapsidation of pgRNA. Fitting our model to the data, we quantify the drug-induced percent inhibition of encapsidated pgRNA production, which we term their in vivo antiviral effectiveness. In both trials, the HBV RNA and HBV DNA declined in a biphasic manner during therapy. The model described these decays well and, by fitting the model to the data, we estimated the CAM effectiveness in each trial participant. Mathematical analysis of the model showed that the magnitude of the first phase of decline of HBV RNA and HBV DNA is explicitly related to CAM effectiveness. However, in the clinic, the end of the first phase may not be known due to sparse sampling. Using clinical trial simulations, we show that the HBV RNA and HBV DNA declines between baseline and day 14 of CAM monotherapy can be used to predict CAM effectiveness. We show that HBV RNA is a clinically relevant biomarker and that very short-term phase I clinical trials can be used to evaluate the in vivo effectiveness of new CAMs, thus reducing the danger of drug resistance developing in trial participants.

abstract_zh: 衣壳组装调节剂 (CAM) 是一类很有前景的 抗病毒药物 治疗,用于治疗 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染。几种 CAM 已在临床试验中进行了评估,但没有简单的方法来评估它们的体内 抗病毒药物 有效性。在两种 CAM(vebicorvir 和 ABI-H2158)的 I 期试验中,我们对 HBV RNA、HBV DNA 和 ALT 的细胞内和细胞外动力学进行了病毒动力学建模,这两种 CAM 抑制 pgRNA 的衣壳化。将我们的模型与数据进行拟合,我们量化了药物诱导的衣壳化 pgRNA 产生的抑制百分比,我们将其称为体内 抗病毒药物 有效性。在这两项试验中,治疗期间 HBV RNA 和 HBV DNA 均呈双相下降。该模型很好地描述了这些衰减,并且通过将模型与数据进行拟合,我们估计了每个试验参与者的 CAM 有效性。该模型的数学分析表明,HBV RNA 和 HBV DNA 第一阶段下降的幅度与 CAM 有效性明确相关。然而,在临床中,由于采样稀疏,第一阶段的结束可能无法得知。通过临床试验模拟,我们表明,从基线到 CAM 单药治疗第 14 天,HBV RNA 和 HBV DNA 下降,可用于预测 CAM 有效性。我们证明,HBV RNA 是一种临床相关的生物标志物,非常短期的 I 期临床试验可用于评估新 CAM 的体内有效性,从而降低试验参与者产生耐药性的危险。

title: HLA-DQB1*06:02 and a critical amino acid variant in protection against occult hepatitis B virus infection
abstract: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system plays a critical role in determining the outcomes of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, yet the genetic mechanisms underlying occult HBV infection (OBI), a form marked by detectable HBV DNA in the absence of hepatitis B surface antigen, remain poorly defined. Here, we performed high-resolution HLA genotyping and amino acid-based association analysis in a Chinese population comprising 239 OBI cases and 545 healthy controls. We identified the HLA class II allele DQB1*06:02 as a protective signal against OBI, with conditional analysis confirming its independent effect. This allele is carried on the conserved haplotype DRB1*15:01~DQA1*02:01~DQB1*06:02, which was significantly underrepresented in OBI cases. Conversely, the DRB1*09:01~DQA1*03:02~DQB1*03:03 haplotype was associated with increased OBI risk. Analysis of the HLA-DQB1 amino acid residues revealed that position 119, located in an α-helix of the peptide-binding groove, drives a substantial portion of the observed association. The phenylalanine variant at this site remained strongly protective after multiple-testing correction and is encoded by DQB1*06:02. Our study thus delineates both allele and amino acid level HLA determinants of OBI susceptibility, highlighting a key structural residue that may influence antigen presentation and immune clearance of HBV. These findings provide a refined genetic framework for understanding host and virus interactions in occult HBV persistence.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Occult hepatitis B virus infection (OBI) persists despite undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen, and the genetic mechanisms underlying host control remain incompletely understood. analysis.methods: High-resolution HLA genotyping and amino acid-based association analysis were conducted to identify HLA class II alleles and structural residues associated with OBI.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated host genetic determinants of occult hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection (OBI) by performing high-resolution HLA genotyping and amino acid-based association analysis in a Chinese cohort of 239 OBI cases and 545 healthy controls. The HLA class II allele DQB1*06:02 was identified as a protective factor against OBI, with its independent effect confirmed through conditional analysis. Conversely, the DRB1*09:01~DQA1*03:02~DQB1*03:03 haplotype was associated with increased OBI risk. Structural analysis revealed that position 119 in the HLA-DQB1 peptide-binding groove, specifically the phenylalanine variant encoded by DQB1*06:02, drove a substantial portion of the association. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that HLA-DQB1*06:02 and the phenylalanine variant at position 119 may influence antigen presentation and immune clearance of HBV, providing a refined genetic framework for understanding occult HBV persistence. The results suggest potential implications for genetic risk stratification and vaccine design, though the study's single-population design and observational nature limit generalisability and functional validation.

abstract_zh: 人类白细胞抗原 (HLA) 系统在确定 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染的结果中发挥着关键作用,但隐匿性 HBV 感染 (OBI) 的遗传机制仍不清楚,隐匿性 HBV 感染 (OBI) 是一种在没有乙型肝炎表面抗原的情况下以可检测到的 HBV DNA 为标志的形式。在这里,我们对包括 239 名 OBI 病例和 545 名健康对照的中国人群进行了高分辨率 HLA 基因分型和基于氨基酸的关联分析。我们将 HLA II 类等位基因 DQB1*06:02 确定为针对 OBI 的保护信号,条件分析证实了其独立作用。该等位基因携带保守的单倍型 DRB1*15:01~DQA1*02:01~DQB1*06:02,在 OBI 病例中明显不足。相反,DRB1*09:01~DQA1*03:02~DQB1*03:03 单倍型与 OBI 风险增加相关。对 HLA-DQB1 氨基酸残基的分析表明,位于肽结合沟 α 螺旋中的位置 119 驱动了所观察到的关联的很大一部分。该位点的苯丙氨酸变体经过多重测试校正后仍然具有很强的保护性,由DQB1*06:02编码。因此,我们的研究描绘了 OBI 易感性的等位基因和氨基酸水平 HLA 决定因素,强调了可能影响 HBV 抗原呈递和免疫清除的关键结构残基。这些发现为理解 宿主 和隐匿性 HBV 持续存在中的病毒相互作用提供了一个完善的遗传框架。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果描述了 OBI 易感性的等位基因和氨基酸水平 HLA 决定因素,强调了可能影响 HBV 抗原呈递和免疫清除的关键结构残基。这为理解隐匿性 HBV 持续存在中的 宿主 病毒相互作用提供了一个精细的遗传框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明 HLA-DQB1*06:02 和第 119 位的苯丙氨酸变体可以为遗传风险分层和针对隐匿性 HBV 感染的 疫苗 设计策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这项研究的局限性在于它只关注单一的中国人群,这可能会限制其对其他种族群体的普遍适用性。证据是中等的,因为它依赖于观察关联,而没有对结构机制进行功能验证。

title: Nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy combined with pegylated interferon α-2b guided by the GOLDEN prediction model for functional cure of chronic hepatitis B: study protocol (GIFT project).
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The limited efficacy and tolerability of interferon (IFN)-based therapies make refining patient selection a critical step towards achieving a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The novel GOLDEN model, based on sequential changes in quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg), accurately predicts hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy. However, it remains unvalidated in patients receiving sequential pegylated IFN α-2b (Peg-IFN α-2b)-based therapy. We aim to validate the GOLDEN model and the optimised cut-off value for the predictive index (Pi) to prospectively identify optimal candidates for clinical cure among patients receiving sequential Peg-IFN α-2b therapy using pre-IFN treatment qHBsAg kinetics across multiple centres. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This prospective multicentre observational cohort study will enrol 300 NA-experienced patients with CHB from 22 centres in China. Patients, stratified by the Pi calculated from pre-treatment qHBsAg dynamics, will be classified into two groups: favourable (Pi>0.15, n=150) and unfavourable candidates (Pi≤0.15, n=150). All patients will receive 48 weeks of combination therapy with Peg-IFN α-2b plus ongoing NAs. The primary endpoint is the HBsAg clearance rate at week 48, with clearance defined as HBsAg loss at any time during the treatment period. Secondary endpoints include HBsAg seroconversion and sustained clearance rates. The sample size provides 80% power to detect a significant difference between the assumed clearance rates (35% vs 20%, favourable vs unfavourable group). Between-group comparisons will be performed using the χ2 or Fisher's exact test. Long-term follow-up studies are warranted to assess sustained HBsAg clearance and its impact on clinical outcomes. Concurrently, we will explore establishing novel predictive models using this framework alongside other baseline indicators. Future research could focus on analysing serial inflammatory cytokine profiles from stored blood samples to elucidate the immunological mechanisms driving treatment response. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study protocol has been reviewed, and ethical approval has been obtained from the ethics committee of Tangdu Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University (approval no. Approval has also been secured from 21 additional participating centres. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2500095819.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aims to refine patient selection for achieving a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) by validating the GOLDEN prediction model, which uses quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) kinetics to identify optimal candidates for therapy.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective strategies for selecting patients for combination therapy, potentially improving the likelihood of achieving a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B.

analysis.summary_en: This study protocol outlines a prospective multicentre observational cohort study aimed at validating the GOLDEN prediction model for identifying optimal candidates for a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy combined with pegylated interferon α-2b (Peg-IFN α-2b). The study will enrol 300 NA-experienced patients with CHB from 22 centres in China, stratified into favourable (Pi>0.15) and unfavourable (Pi≤0.15) groups based on pre-treatment quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) dynamics. The primary endpoint is HBsAg clearance at week 48, with secondary endpoints including HBsAg seroconversion and sustained clearance rates. The study will use χ2 or Fisher's exact tests for between-group comparisons and aims to provide 80% power to detect a significant difference between clearance rates (35% vs 20%). The GOLDEN model, which uses sequential qHBsAg changes, is interpreted as accurately predicting HBsAg loss in CHB patients on NA therapy. The findings may inform improved patient selection strategies for combination therapy. However, the study is limited to a single model and lacks long-term follow-up data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过验证 GOLDEN 预测模型来完善患者选择,以实现 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 中的 功能性治愈,该模型使用定量 HBsAg (qHBsAg) 动力学来识别最佳治疗候选者。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项前瞻性多中心观察性 队列研究 研究,招募了来自中国 22 个中心的 300 名有 NA 经验的 CHB 患者。根据 治疗 前 qHBsAg 动态计算得出的预测指数 (Pi) 将患者分为两组:有利候选者 (Pi>0.15,n=150) 和不利候选者 (Pi≤0.15,n=150)。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究将对 48 周以上的所有患者使用 Peg-IFN α-2b 加持续核苷(酸)类似物 (NA) 的联合疗法。组间比较将使用 χ2 或 Fisher 精确检验进行。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要终点是第 48 周时的 HBsAg 清除率,清除率定义为 治疗 期间任何时间的 HBsAg 消失。样本量提供 80% 的功效来检测假设清除率之间的显着差异(35% 与 20%,有利组与不利组)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: GOLDEN 模型基于 qHBsAg 的连续变化,可以准确预测接受 NA 治疗的慢性乙型肝炎患者的 HBsAg 消失。该研究将探索使用该框架和其他基线指标建立新颖的预测模型。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为制定更有效的策略来选择患者进行联合治疗提供信息,从而有可能提高在 慢性乙型肝炎 中实现 功能性治愈 的可能性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单一预测模型,不包括长期随访数据。证据是中等的,因为它基于具有明确样本量和统计分析的前瞻性观察设计。

abstract_zh: 简介:基于干扰素 (IFN) 的疗法的疗效和耐受性有限,使得完善患者选择成为 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 实现 功能性治愈 的关键一步。新型 GOLDEN 模型基于 HBsAg (qHBsAg) 定量的连续变化,准确预测接受核苷(酸)类似物 (NA) 治疗的慢性乙型肝炎患者的乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 损失。然而,在接受序贯聚乙二醇化 IFN α-2b (Peg-IFN α-2b) 治疗的患者中,该方法仍未得到验证。我们的目标是验证 GOLDEN 模型和预测指数 (Pi) 的优化截止值,以前瞻性地在多个中心使用前 IFN 治疗 qHBsAg 动力学接受序贯 Peg-IFN α-2b 治疗的患者中确定临床治愈的最佳候选者。方法和分析:这项前瞻性多中心观察性 队列研究 研究将招募来自中国 22 个中心的 300 名有 NA 经验的 CHB 患者。根据 治疗 前 qHBsAg 动态计算得出的 Pi 进行分层的患者将被分为两组:有利候选者(Pi>0.15,n=150)和不利候选者(Pi≤0.15,n=150)。所有患者将接受 48 周的 Peg-IFN α-2b 联合持续 NA 联合治疗。主要终点是第 48 周时的 HBsAg 清除率,清除率定义为 治疗 期间任何时间的 HBsAg 消失。次要终点包括 HBsAg 血清转化和持续清除率。样本量提供 80% 的功效来检测假设清除率之间的显着差异(35% 与 20%,有利组与不利组)。组间比较将使用 χ2 或 Fisher 精确检验进行。有必要进行长期随访研究来评估持续的 HBsAg 清除及其对临床结果的影响。同时,我们将探索使用该框架和其他基线指标建立新颖的预测模型。未来的研究可能集中于分析储存的血液样本中的一系列炎症细胞因子谱,以阐明驱动 治疗 反应的免疫机制。伦理与传播:研究方案已经过审查,并获得了第四军医大学唐都医院伦理委员会的伦理批准(批准号。还获得了另外 21 个参与中心的批准。试验注册号:ChiCTR2500095819。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为制定更有效的策略来选择患者进行联合治疗提供信息,从而有可能提高在 慢性乙型肝炎 中实现 功能性治愈 的可能性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单一预测模型,不包括长期随访数据。证据是中等的,因为它基于具有明确样本量和统计分析的前瞻性观察设计。

title: Drug resistance mutations of hepatitis B virus (HBV) influence the yield of the virions of the human hepatitis delta virus (HDV) and their infectivity
abstract: ABSTRACT This work analyzed 30 drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBV) (i.e., HBsAg) selected by several FDA-approved anti-HBV nucleos(t)ide analogs. All DRM-bearing HBsAg variants supported the formation and secretion of hepatitis delta virus (HDV), and only 13/30 DRMs considerably decreased the yield of secreted HDV virions. However, the majority of DRMs (23/30) greatly reduced HDV infectivity, and four of them even caused the complete loss of infectivity, which was determined by analyzing the levels of HDV RNA genomes in the infected cells, and the fraction of HDV-infected cells. The ability to inhibit HDV infectivity was observed for DRMs located in the large cytosolic loop (LCL), major antigenic loop (MAL), HDV-binding site (HDV-BS), and the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg, which suggested that DRMs mediate their inhibitory influence by both direct and indirect mechanisms that could alter the attachment/entry, post-entry trafficking, and/or subsequent uncoating of the virions. This report also established the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV as critical regulators of the overall infectivity of HDV virions. It became apparent that in the settings of natural HBV/HDV infection, DRMs can therefore greatly reduce the spread/superinfection of HDV and diminish the size of the HDV reservoir in chronically infected livers. Overall, our findings advanced the understanding of how anti-HBV drug treatments influence the HDV life cycle, the roles of HBV envelope proteins in facilitating the assembly and infectivity of HDV, and the mechanism of complex HBV-HDV interactions. IMPORTANCE The study showed that the drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBsAg) can greatly reduce hepatitis delta virus (HDV) assembly and infectivity. Since most of the tested DRMs considerably reduced HDV infectivity, and four of them resulted in a complete loss of the infectivity, such effects can lead to suppression of HDV spread/superinfection and reduction of the HDV reservoir in the infected liver. If most detrimental for infectivity DRMs are present on the majority of HBsAg molecules, this could facilitate substantial suppression of chronic HDV infection and possibly reduce HDV-associated liver pathogenesis. It was also determined that DRMs located in the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg could critically alter HDV infectivity. Our findings therefore suggest that different HBsAg regions work in the intramolecular coordinating concert, facilitating the assembly and infectivity of the virions, and that certain short- and long-distance interactions between different regions of HBsAg take place.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate how drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBV) affect the assembly and infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV). The background highlights the importance of understanding these interactions to improve therapeutic strategies for HBV/HDV co-infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 30 DRMs in HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) selected by FDA-approved anti-HBV nucleos(t)ide analogs. These DRMs were tested for their impact on HDV assembly and infectivity in a controlled experimental setting.
analysis.methods: The researchers examined the ability of DRM-bearing HBsAg variants to support HDV formation and secretion by analyzing HDV RNA genome levels and the fraction of HDV-infected cells. They also identified the specific regions of HBsAg where DRMs exerted their effects.
analysis.main_results: All DRM-bearing HBsAg variants supported HDV formation and secretion, but only 13/30 DRMs significantly reduced the yield of secreted HDV virions. Additionally, 23/30 DRMs greatly reduced HDV infectivity, with four causing a complete loss of infectivity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that DRMs in specific regions of HBsAg can inhibit HDV infectivity through direct and indirect mechanisms, altering virion attachment/entry, trafficking, and uncoating. They also identified transmembrane domains II, III, and IV as critical regulators of HDV infectivity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that anti-HBV drug treatments may influence HDV life cycle and reduce HDV spread/superinfection, potentially leading to a decrease in HDV-associated liver pathogenesis in chronically infected individuals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, and the evidence is based on experimental observations of DRM effects on HDV. The confidence in these findings is moderate due to the lack of detailed experimental data and broader clinical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBV) affect the assembly and infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV). title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 的耐药性影响人丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 病毒粒子的产量及其传染性
source_body_en: ABSTRACT This work analyzed 30 drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBV) (i.e., HBsAg) selected by several FDA-approved anti-HBV nucleos(t)ide analogs. All DRM-bearing HBsAg variants supported the formation and secretion of hepatitis delta virus (HDV), and only 13/30 DRMs considerably decreased the yield of secreted HDV virions. However, the majority of DRMs (23/30) greatly reduced HDV infectivity, and four of them even caused the complete loss of infectivity, which was determined by analyzing the levels of HDV RNA genomes in the infected cells, and the fraction of HDV-infected cells. The ability to inhibit HDV infectivity was observed for DRMs located in the large cytosolic loop (LCL), major antigenic loop (MAL), HDV-binding site (HDV-BS), and the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg, which suggested that DRMs mediate their inhibitory influence by both direct and indirect mechanisms that could alter the attachment/entry, post-entry trafficking, and/or subsequent uncoating of the virions. This report also established the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV as critical regulators of the overall infectivity of HDV virions. It became apparent that in the settings of natural HBV/HDV infection, DRMs can therefore greatly reduce the spread/superinfection of HDV and diminish the size of the HDV reservoir in chronically infected livers. Overall, our findings advanced the understanding of how anti-HBV drug treatments influence the HDV life cycle, the roles of HBV envelope proteins in facilitating the assembly and infectivity of HDV, and the mechanism of complex HBV-HDV interactions. IMPORTANCE The study showed that the drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBsAg) can greatly reduce hepatitis delta virus (HDV) assembly and infectivity. Since most of the tested DRMs considerably reduced HDV infectivity, and four of them resulted in a complete loss of the infectivity, such effects can lead to suppression of HDV spread/superinfection and reduction of the HDV reservoir in the infected liver. If most detrimental for infectivity DRMs are present on the majority of HBsAg molecules, this could facilitate substantial suppression of chronic HDV infection and possibly reduce HDV-associated liver pathogenesis. It was also determined that DRMs located in the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg could critically alter HDV infectivity. Our findings therefore suggest that different HBsAg regions work in the intramolecular coordinating concert, facilitating the assembly and infectivity of the virions, and that certain short- and long-distance interactions between different regions of HBsAg take place.
abstract_zh: 摘要 这项工作分析了由 FDA 批准的几种抗 HBV 核苷类似物选择的 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 表面抗原(即 HBsAg)中的 30 种耐药性 突变 (DRM)。所有携带 DRM 的 HBsAg 变体都支持丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 的形成和分泌,只有 13/30 DRM 显着降低了分泌的 HDV 病毒粒子的产量。然而,大多数DRM(23/30)大大降低了HDV的感染性,其中四种甚至导致感染性完全丧失,这是通过分析感染细胞中HDV RNA 基因组的水平以及HDV感染细胞的比例来确定的。观察到位于大胞质环 (LCL)、主要抗原环 (MAL)、HDV 结合位点 (HDV-BS) 和 HBsAg 跨膜结构域 II、III 和 IV 中的 DRM 具有抑制 HDV 感染性的能力,这表明 DRM 通过直接和间接机制介导其抑制影响,这些机制可能改变病毒粒子的附着/进入、进入后运输和/或随后的脱壳。该报告还确立了跨膜结构域 II、III 和 IV 作为 HDV 病毒粒子整体感染性的关键调节因子。很明显,在自然 HBV/HDV 感染的情况下,DRM 可以大大减少 HDV 的传播/重复感染,并缩小慢性感染肝脏中 HDV 储存宿主 的大小。总体而言,我们的研究结果加深了对抗 HBV 药物 治疗 如何影响 HDV 生命周期、HBV 包膜蛋白在促进 HDV 组装和感染性中的作用以及复杂 HBV-HDV 相互作用机制的理解。重要性 研究表明,乙型肝炎病毒(HBsAg)表面抗原中的耐药性突变(DRMs)可以大大降低丁型肝炎病毒(HDV)的组装和传染性。由于大多数测试的 DRM 显着降低了 HDV 感染性,其中四种导致感染性完全丧失,因此这种作用可以抑制 HDV 传播/重复感染,并减少受感染肝脏中的 HDV 储存宿主。如果对感染性最有害的 DRM 存在于大多数 HBsAg 分子上,这可能有助于显着抑制慢性 HDV 感染,并可能减少 HDV 相关肝脏 发病机制。还确定位于 HBsAg 跨膜域 II、III 和 IV 中的 DRM 可以严重改变 HDV 感染性。因此,我们的研究结果表明,不同的 HBsAg 区域在分子内协调作用中发挥作用,促进病毒体的组装和感染性,并且 HBsAg 不同区域之间发生某些短距离和长距离相互作用。

title: Dynamics on Hepatitis B Virus Infection In Vivo with Immune Noise and Interval Delay
abstract: Immune delay and noise are ubiquitous in the evolution of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in vivo . A stochastic HBV infection dynamic model is proposed to investigate the interaction effects of interval delay and white noise during the immune phase. Global existence, nonnegativity, and boundedness of the solutions are obtained. The stochastic reproduction number is derived, which serves as a threshold determining viral extinction or persistence within-host. Furthermore, the stability conditions for the first and second moments are established. Numerical simulations, employing time-series analysis, confirm the existence of stochastic periodicity. Compared to the deterministic model, noise induces an earlier onset of stochastic periodicity. However, based on the expectation stability of the sample trajectories, as the Hopf bifurcation of the corresponding deterministic system has not yet occurred, the noise-induced early periodicity is likely a temporary phenomenon rather than a true periodic behavior.

source_body_en: Immune delay and noise are ubiquitous in the evolution of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in vivo . A stochastic HBV infection dynamic model is proposed to investigate the interaction effects of interval delay and white noise during the immune phase. Global existence, nonnegativity, and boundedness of the solutions are obtained. The stochastic reproduction number is derived, which serves as a threshold determining viral extinction or persistence within-host. Furthermore, the stability conditions for the first and second moments are established. Numerical simulations, employing time-series analysis, confirm the existence of stochastic periodicity. Compared to the deterministic model, noise induces an earlier onset of stochastic periodicity. However, based on the expectation stability of the sample trajectories, as the Hopf bifurcation of the corresponding deterministic system has not yet occurred, the noise-induced early periodicity is likely a temporary phenomenon rather than a true periodic behavior.

title: Global stability of two-patch within-host HBV infection dynamics with unidirectional viral spread
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infects liver cells (hepatocytes). Persistent HBV infection may lead to the development of abnormal nodular formations within liver tissue. In this study, we propose and analyze a mathematical model describing the dynamics of a two-patch within-host HBV infection with unidirectional viral transmission from patch-1 to patch-2. The model captures interactions among six compartments: uninfected hepatocytes, infected hepatocytes, and free HBV particles in each of the two patches. A comprehensive mathematical analysis is carried out, including proofs of non-negativity and boundedness of solutions. The basic reproduction numbers in patch-1 \(\left(R_{1}\right)\) and patch-2 \(\left(R_{2}\right)\) are calculated using the next generation method. The global stability of all equilibrium points is rigorously examined using Lyapunov functions and LaSalle’s invariance principle. Numerical simulations are conducted, demonstrating strong agreement with the analytical findings. Finally, sensitivity analysis identifies the key parameters influencing viral persistence.
journal: International Journal of Analysis and Applications

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for a deeper understanding of within-host dynamics during hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, particularly the mechanisms underlying viral persistence and spread across spatially distinct liver regions. It highlights the gap in mathematical modeling of HBV infection across multiple liver patches and frames the objective to analyze such dynamics with unidirectional viral transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors propose and analyze a mathematical model describing two-patch within-host HBV infection dynamics with unidirectional viral spread from patch-1 to patch-2. The model conceptualizes interactions among six compartments: uninfected hepatocytes, infected hepatocytes, and free HBV particles in each of the two patches.
analysis.methods: The study employs a mathematical modeling approach to analyze HBV infection dynamics, including the calculation of basic reproduction numbers (R1 and R2) for each patch using the next generation method. Global stability of equilibrium points is examined through rigorous proofs using Lyapunov functions and LaSalle’s invariance principle.
analysis.main_results: The basic reproduction numbers in patch-1 (R1) and patch-2 (R2) are calculated using the next generation method. Global stability of all equilibrium points is rigorously examined using Lyapunov functions and LaSalle’s invariance principle.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating the feasibility of modeling HBV within-host dynamics across spatially distinct liver regions and identifying conditions for viral persistence or clearance. The novelty lies in the rigorous mathematical analysis of global stability and the explicit consideration of unidirectional viral transmission between patches.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted antiviral strategies by identifying key parameters influencing viral persistence, potentially guiding treatment optimization for chronic HBV infection. The model may also contribute to understanding the spatial heterogeneity of HBV infection within the liver.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level descriptions and lacks empirical validation or clinical data, which constrains the strength of the conclusions. The study relies solely on mathematical modeling and theoretical analysis, without experimental or observational corroboration.

analysis.summary_en: This study proposes a two-patch mathematical model to analyze within-host hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection dynamics with unidirectional viral spread from one liver region to another. The model includes six compartments representing uninfected hepatocytes, infected hepatocytes, and free HBV particles in each patch. Using the next generation method, the authors calculate basic reproduction numbers for each patch and rigorously examine global stability of equilibrium points via Lyapunov functions and LaSalle’s invariance principle. The work highlights the feasibility of modeling spatial HBV dynamics and identifies conditions for viral persistence or clearance. While mathematically rigorous, the study is limited to theoretical analysis without empirical validation, which constrains the strength of its conclusions and public health implications.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for a deeper understanding of within-host dynamics during hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, particularly the mechanisms underlying viral persistence and spread across spatially distinct liver regions. It highlights the gap in mathematical modeling of HBV infection across multiple liver patches and frames the objective to analyze such dynamics with unidirectional viral transmission.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The authors propose and analyze a mathematical model describing two-patch within-host HBV infection dynamics with unidirectional viral spread from patch-1 to patch-2. The model conceptualizes interactions among six compartments: uninfected hepatocytes, infected hepatocytes, and free HBV particles in each of the two patches.
elements_en.methods: The study employs a mathematical modeling approach to analyze HBV infection dynamics, including the calculation of basic reproduction numbers (R1 and R2) for each patch using the next generation method. Global stability of equilibrium points is examined through rigorous proofs using Lyapunov functions and LaSalle’s invariance principle.
elements_en.main_results: The basic reproduction numbers in patch-1 (R1) and patch-2 (R2) are calculated using the next generation method. Global stability of all equilibrium points is rigorously examined using Lyapunov functions and LaSalle’s invariance principle.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating the feasibility of modeling HBV within-host dynamics across spatially distinct liver regions and identifying conditions for viral persistence or clearance. The novelty lies in the rigorous mathematical analysis of global stability and the explicit consideration of unidirectional viral transmission between patches.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted antiviral strategies by identifying key parameters influencing viral persistence, potentially guiding treatment optimization for chronic HBV infection. The model may also contribute to understanding the spatial heterogeneity of HBV infection within the liver.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level descriptions and lacks empirical validation or clinical data, which constrains the strength of the conclusions. The study relies solely on mathematical modeling and theoretical analysis, without experimental or observational corroboration.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了更深入了解 宿主 (HBV) 感染期间 宿主 动态的需要,特别是病毒持久性和跨空间不同肝脏区域传播的机制。它强调了跨多个肝脏斑块的 HBV 感染数学模型的差距,并制定了使用单向病毒 传播 分析这种动态的目标。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 作者提出并分析了一个数学模型,该模型描述了 宿主 内两个补丁的 HBV 感染动态,以及从补丁 1 到补丁 2 的单向病毒传播。该模型概念化了六个区室之间的相互作用:未感染的肝细胞、感染的肝细胞以及两个斑块中的游离 HBV 颗粒。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用数学建模方法来分析 HBV 感染动态,包括使用下一代方法计算每个斑块的基本繁殖数(R1 和 R2)。通过使用李亚普诺夫函数和拉萨尔不变原理的严格证明来检验平衡点的全局稳定性。
elements_zh.main_results: patch-1 (R1) 和 patch-2 (R2) 中的基本再现数是使用下一代方法计算的。使用李雅普诺夫函数和拉萨尔不变原理严格检验所有平衡点的全局稳定性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了对跨空间不同肝脏区域的 宿主 内的 HBV 动态进行建模并确定病毒持续存在或清除的条件的可行性。新颖之处在于对全局稳定性的严格数学分析以及补丁之间单向病毒 传播 的明确考虑。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以通过确定影响病毒持久性的关键参数,为制定有针对性的 抗病毒药物 策略提供信息,从而可能指导慢性 HBV 感染的 治疗 优化。该模型还可能有助于了解肝脏内 HBV 感染的空间异质性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于抽象级别的描述,缺乏经验验证或临床数据,这限制了结论的强度。该研究仅依赖于数学模型和理论分析,没有实验或观察佐证。

title_zh: 宿主 HBV 感染动态中两个补丁的全局稳定性与单向病毒传播
source_body_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infects liver cells (hepatocytes). Persistent HBV infection may lead to the development of abnormal nodular formations within liver tissue. In this study, we propose and analyze a mathematical model describing the dynamics of a two-patch within-host HBV infection with unidirectional viral transmission from patch-1 to patch-2. The model captures interactions among six compartments: uninfected hepatocytes, infected hepatocytes, and free HBV particles in each of the two patches. A comprehensive mathematical analysis is carried out, including proofs of non-negativity and boundedness of solutions. The basic reproduction numbers in patch-1 \(\left(R_{1}\right)\) and patch-2 \(\left(R_{2}\right)\) are calculated using the next generation method. The global stability of all equilibrium points is rigorously examined using Lyapunov functions and LaSalle’s invariance principle. Numerical simulations are conducted, demonstrating strong agreement with the analytical findings. Finally, sensitivity analysis identifies the key parameters influencing viral persistence.
abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染肝细胞(肝细胞)。持续的乙型肝炎病毒感染可能导致肝组织内形成异常结节。在本研究中,我们提出并分析了一个数学模型,该模型描述了从补丁 1 到补丁 2 的单向病毒 传播 内 宿主 HBV 感染的两个补丁的动态。该模型捕获了六个区室之间的相互作用:未感染的肝细胞、感染的肝细胞以及两个斑块中每个区中的游离 HBV 颗粒。进行了全面的数学分析,包括解的非负性和有界性证明。patch-1 \(\left(R_{1}\right)\) 和 patch-2 \(\left(R_{2}\right)\) 中的基本再生数是使用下一代方法计算的。使用李亚普诺夫函数和拉萨尔不变原理严格检验所有平衡点的全局稳定性。进行了数值模拟,表明与分析结果非常一致。最后,敏感性分析确定了影响病毒持久性的关键参数。

title: Characterising Hepatitis D Virus in the UK From 2011 to 2021.
abstract: Little is known about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK. HDV screening is recommended among all individuals with HBV, with coinfection associated with increased disease progression. Using data on HDV testing, shared by 11 laboratories in the UK who reported undertaking HDV testing, and national testing data for HBV we established a cohort of individuals tested for HDV, investigating testing pathways, describing characteristics and outcomes of those HDV-RNA positive to inform targeted interventions for testing, diagnosis and linkage to care. Demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment and recent laboratory results from NHS trusts, and through linkage to national healthcare datasets was collected for HDV-RNA positive individuals. Between 2011 and 2021, 42% of individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England were linked to an HDV test. Anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. HDV-RNA positivity in the absence of an anti-HDV result was 6.4%. Among individuals who were HDV-RNA positive, 94.3% were non-UK born, with 24 different primary languages reported, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis. 10% had died of which 58.4% died of liver disease. In conclusion, our findings indicate that HDV testing in HBV positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal against testing guidelines, including RNA testing among those who are anti-HDV positive. Considerable work is needed to improve the patient care pathway, to ensure patients are appropriately diagnosed, linked and retained in care, with adequate access to treatment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the lack of knowledge about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK, highlighting a gap in understanding testing practices and clinical outcomes among HBV-infected individuals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using HDV testing data from 11 UK laboratories and national HBV testing data to establish a cohort of individuals tested for HDV between 2011 and 2021.
analysis.methods: The study collected demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment records, and laboratory results from NHS trusts and national healthcare datasets for HDV-RNA positive individuals.
analysis.main_results: Among individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England, 42% were linked to an HDV test; anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested, and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. Among HDV-RNA positive individuals, 94.3% were non-UK born, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that HDV testing in HBV-positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal compared to testing guidelines, including RNA testing among anti-HDV positive cases, indicating a need for improved diagnostic pathways.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve HDV testing, diagnosis, and linkage to care among HBV-infected individuals in the UK to reduce disease progression and mortality.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on retrospective data from a limited number of laboratories, which may not capture all testing pathways or outcomes, and the evidence strength is moderate due to potential selection and reporting biases.

analysis.summary_en: This UK study examined HDV testing practices and outcomes among HBV-infected individuals from 2011 to 2021 using data from 11 laboratories and national HBV testing records. It found that only 42% of newly diagnosed HBV cases were linked to HDV testing, with 5.0% anti-HDV positivity and 45.7% ever HDV-RNA positive among those tested. Among HDV-RNA positive individuals, 94.3% were non-UK born, 49% received treatment, and 48% had cirrhosis, with 10% deceased, primarily from liver disease. The authors interpret these results as indicating sub-optimal HDV testing compared to guidelines, underscoring the need for improved diagnostic pathways, linkage to care, and treatment access to mitigate disease progression.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了英国对 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 双重感染缺乏了解的问题,突显了 HBV 感染者在了解检测实践和临床结果方面的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用来自 11 个英国实验室的 HDV 检测数据和国家 HBV 检测数据进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究,以建立 2011 年至 2021 年间接受 HDV 检测的个体的 队列研究。

title_zh: 2011 年至 2021 年英国丁型肝炎病毒的特征。
source_body_en: Little is known about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK. HDV screening is recommended among all individuals with HBV, with coinfection associated with increased disease progression. Using data on HDV testing, shared by 11 laboratories in the UK who reported undertaking HDV testing, and national testing data for HBV we established a cohort of individuals tested for HDV, investigating testing pathways, describing characteristics and outcomes of those HDV-RNA positive to inform targeted interventions for testing, diagnosis and linkage to care. Demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment and recent laboratory results from NHS trusts, and through linkage to national healthcare datasets was collected for HDV-RNA positive individuals. Between 2011 and 2021, 42% of individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England were linked to an HDV test. Anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. HDV-RNA positivity in the absence of an anti-HDV result was 6.4%. Among individuals who were HDV-RNA positive, 94.3% were non-UK born, with 24 different primary languages reported, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis. 10% had died of which 58.4% died of liver disease. In conclusion, our findings indicate that HDV testing in HBV positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal against testing guidelines, including RNA testing among those who are anti-HDV positive. Considerable work is needed to improve the patient care pathway, to ensure patients are appropriately diagnosed, linked and retained in care, with adequate access to treatment.
abstract_zh: 在英国,人们对 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 的双重感染知之甚少。建议对所有 HBV 感染者进行 HDV 筛查,因为合并感染会导致疾病进展加快。利用英国 11 个报告进行 HDV 检测的实验室共享的 HDV 检测数据以及全国 HBV 检测数据,我们建立了 HDV 检测个体的 队列研究,调查检测途径,描述 HDV-RNA 阳性的特征和结果,为检测、诊断 和护理联系的针对性干预措施提供信息。我们收集了 HDV-RNA 阳性个体的人口统计信息、临床评估、治疗 和 NHS 信托机构的最新实验室结果,并通过与国家医疗保健数据集的链接来收集。2011 年至 2021 年间,英格兰新诊断出的 HBV 患者中有 42% 与 HDV 检测有关。抗 HDV 阳性率为 5.0%,55.8% 进行过 HDV-RNA 检测,45.7% 曾经呈 HDV-RNA 阳性。在没有抗 HDV 结果的情况下,HDV-RNA 阳性率为 6.4%。在 HDV-RNA 阳性的个体中,94.3% 为非英国出生,报告有 24 种不同的主要语言,49% 有 治疗 证据,48% 有肝硬化证据。10%的人死于肝病,其中58.4%死于肝病。总之,我们的研究结果表明,在英国,针对 HBV 阳性个体的 HDV 检测相对于检测指南(包括抗 HDV 阳性者的 RNA 检测)来说并不是最佳的。需要做大量的工作来改善患者护理途径,以确保患者得到适当的诊断、联系和保留护理,并有足够的机会获得 治疗。

title: HBsAg glycan isomer: a potential circulating biomarker for monitoring cccDNA and predicting virologic response in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Background Previous research has identified that Hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) specifically marks O-glycosylated M-HBsAg exclusively present on infectious Dane particles (unlike total HBsAg, which is dominated by non-infectious subviral particles), it offers a more specific association with infectious viral burden and cccDNA activity. Accordingly, the present study aims to assess the potential of HBsAgGi as a circulating biomarker to reflect intrahepatic covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) and transcriptional activity, and for monitoring antiviral response. Methods A total of 73 individuals diagnosed with chronic genotype C HBV infection were recruited for this study. Serum concentrations of HBsAgGi, HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA, and HBV RNA were measured. Intrahepatic cccDNA and HBV RNA loads were determined in liver biopsy specimens obtained from 16 patients. Correlations between serum HBsAgGi and intrahepatic markers were analyzed. We measured serum Hepatitis B core-related antigen (HBcrAg) levels in 28 patients. 18 patients received nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy for 48 weeks and we evaluated levels of HBsAgGi after therapy. Additionally, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was conducted to assess the discriminative ability of the candidate biomarkers in predicting virological response (VR). Results Serum HBsAgGi demonstrated significant positive correlations with intrahepatic cccDNA (r = 0.7172, P < 0.01), HBV RNA (r = 0.7879, P < 0.01), and the RNA/cccDNA ratio (r = 0.5840, P < 0.05), showing stronger correlations than conventional serum markers (HBcrAg, HBV RNA, DNA, HBsAg). HBsAgGi also showed the strongest correlation with serum HBcrAg (r = 0.5361, P < 0.01) in 28 patients. During treatment, HBsAgGi levels declined and baseline HBsAgGi predicted VR with superior accuracy (AUC = 0.9538) versus other markers. Conclusion Serum HBsAgGi represents an emerging, minimally invasive serum indicator for assessing intrahepatic cccDNA loads and viral transcriptional activity, demonstrating stronger correlations with intrahepatic markers compared to conventional serum markers in this cohort. It also shows promising utility for predicting treatment response.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B remains difficult to monitor because conventional serum markers reflect both infectious and non-infectious viral components. The study was needed to determine whether the Hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi)—which marks O-glycosylated M-HBsAg on infectious Dane particles—can serve as a more specific circulating biomarker for intrahepatic cccDNA activity and antiviral response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort of 73 individuals with chronic genotype C HBV infection was enrolled. Serum HBsAgGi, HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA, HBV RNA and HBcrAg were quantified. Intrahepatic cccDNA and HBV RNA were measured in liver biopsy specimens from 16 patients, and HBcrAg was measured in 28 patients.
analysis.methods: Serum concentrations of HBsAgGi and other markers were measured, and intrahepatic cccDNA and HBV RNA loads were determined from liver biopsies. Correlations between serum HBsAgGi and intrahepatic markers were analyzed. ROC curve analysis assessed the discriminative ability of candidate biomarkers in predicting virological response after 48 weeks of nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy in 18 patients.
analysis.main_results: Serum HBsAgGi showed significant positive correlations with intrahepatic cccDNA (r = 0.7172, P < 0.01), HBV RNA (r = 0.7879, P < 0.01), and the RNA/cccDNA ratio (r = 0.5840, P < 0.05), outperforming conventional serum markers. HBsAgGi also correlated strongly with serum HBcrAg (r = 0.5361, P < 0.01) in 28 patients. Baseline HBsAgGi predicted virological response with an AUC of 0.9538.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret HBsAgGi as an emerging, minimally invasive serum indicator that more closely reflects intrahepatic cccDNA loads and transcriptional activity than conventional markers. They highlight its superior predictive utility for treatment response in this cohort.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest HBsAgGi could improve monitoring of cccDNA activity and early prediction of antiviral response in chronic hepatitis B, potentially guiding treatment decisions and follow-up strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its modest sample size, single-cohort design, and reliance on liver biopsy data from only 16 patients, which constrains generalizability. Evidence strength is assessed as moderate pending validation in larger, multi-center cohorts.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated whether the Hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) can serve as a minimally invasive biomarker for intrahepatic cccDNA activity and antiviral response in chronic hepatitis B. In 73 patients with chronic genotype C HBV infection, serum HBsAgGi showed stronger correlations with intrahepatic cccDNA (r = 0.7172, P < 0.01) and HBV RNA (r = 0.7879, P < 0.01) than conventional markers, and predicted virological response with an AUC of 0.9538 after 48 weeks of nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. HBsAgGi also correlated with serum HBcrAg (r = 0.5361, P < 0.01) in 28 patients. The authors conclude that HBsAgGi is a promising serum indicator for monitoring cccDNA activity and predicting treatment response, though the evidence is limited by small sample size and single-cohort design.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎 仍然难以监测,因为传统的血清标记物反映了感染性和非感染性病毒成分。这项研究需要确定乙型肝炎表面抗原聚糖异构体 (HBsAgGi)(在感染性 Dane 颗粒上标记 O-糖基化 M-HBsAg)是否可以作为肝内 共价闭合环状DNA 活性和 抗病毒药物 反应的更特异的循环生物标志物。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 队列研究 纳入了 73 名慢性 C 基因型 HBV 感染者。对血清 HBsAgGi、HBsAg、HBeAg、HBV DNA、HBV RNA 和 HBcrAg 进行定量。对 16 名患者的肝活检标本进行了肝内 共价闭合环状DNA 和 HBV RNA 检测,对 28 名患者进行了 HBcrAg 检测。
elements_zh.methods: 测量了 HBsAgGi 和其他标志物的血清浓度,并通过肝活检测定了肝内 共价闭合环状DNA 和 HBV RNA 载量。分析血清 HBsAgGi 与肝内标志物之间的相关性。ROC 曲线分析评估了候选生物标志物在预测 18 名患者接受 48 周核苷(酸)类似物治疗后病毒学反应的辨别能力。
elements_zh.main_results: 血清HBsAgGi与肝内共价闭合环状DNA(r = 0.7172,P < 0.01)、HBV RNA(r = 0.7879,P < 0.01)和RNA/共价闭合环状DNA比值(r = 0.5840,P < 0.05)呈显着正相关,优于传统血清标志物。在 28 名患者中,HBsAgGi 还与血清 HBcrAg 密切相关(r = 0.5361,P < 0.01)。基线 HBsAgGi 预测病毒学反应,AUC 为 0.9538。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 HBsAgGi 解释为一种新兴的微创血清指标,与传统标记物相比,它更能反映肝内 共价闭合环状DNA 负荷和转录活性。他们在此 队列研究 中强调了其对 治疗 响应的卓越预测实用性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明 HBsAgGi 可以改善对 共价闭合环状DNA 活动的监测以及 慢性乙型肝炎 中 抗病毒药物 反应的早期预测,可能指导 治疗 决策和后续策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量较小、单一 队列研究 设计以及仅依赖 16 名患者的肝活检数据的限制,从而限制了普遍性。证据强度被评估为中等,有待在更大的多中心 队列研究 中进行验证。
